chapters.title: Chapter 525
paragraphs: The Alliance Leader’s Hall was silent. Only one person remained where countless people had come and gone just one shichen—approximately two hours—earlier.
“How quickly the years pass.”

Sword Saint Mae Jonghak murmured the words under his breath. His youthful face was turned toward empty space, but his gaze was searching a distant past. Few people alive still shared those old memories.
They’re all gone now.
Of those who shared Mae Jonghak’s memories, very few had lived out their natural spans. Most had fallen in nameless wastelands and fields, never to rise again.
The monster known as the Great Faction War had claimed countless lives and turned the survivors into heroes.
But in the end... here we are again.
Enough time had passed for the mountains and rivers to change four times over.
Peace had come to the world. The pain and sorrow of war had faded, and orthodox Murim had sung of the glory of victory.
Then a dark cloud called Dark Heaven appeared in a sky that had seemed destined to remain blue forever.
Peace is over.
The runny-nosed child who had not understood the horrors of war had become middle-aged, while the young man who had drawn his weapon and burned with righteous indignation had grown old.
Those who had not even been born back then had come to Henan seeking glory rather than justice.
Their lives, personalities, and goals were all different.
And Sword Saint Mae Jonghak knew it well. He—and no one else—would have to lead them all into battle once again. He would have to defeat Dark Heaven, which sought to plunge the world into misery.
That was when a low voice slipped between Mae Jonghak’s firmly closed lips.
“Every now and then, I wonder whether I can truly do it.”
He was not talking to himself. Mae Jonghak knew it, and so did the person who had been quietly standing guard by the door.
Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho, a sturdy old man, stepped forward as he answered.
“You can.”
Clack.
The tip of his prosthetic leg struck the floor, the sound echoing unusually loudly. Beneath his hanging white hair, his shrewd eyes shone with force.
“No—you must.”
“I know.”
Mae Jonghak let out a quiet sigh.
“But I’ve known nothing but the sword my entire life. That’s how I came by the empty title of Sword Saint.”
“It’s precisely because you are the Sword Saint that everyone will trust and follow you.”
“Being a martial artist is different from being a leader. I never even became the Sect Leader of a single faction.”
“It’s not that you couldn’t. You chose not to.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox was right.
When the Great Faction War ended and Huashan’s former Sect Leader passed away, every disciple of Huashan had been certain that Sword Saint Mae Jonghak would become their new Sect Leader.
“But you refused. In the end, the Sect Leader’s Command Token went to your Disciple, Heavenly Sword True Person.”
“It was only natural. He was more suited to becoming Huashan’s Sect Leader than I was. And...”
Mae Jonghak ran his fingers over the treasured sword at his waist before continuing.
“I simply liked the sword.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox gazed quietly at Mae Jonghak, then suddenly spoke.
“I don’t know if I ever told you this.”
“Told me what?”
“That person once struggled with the same concern.”
“If you mean that person... surely you’re talking about the Martial God?”
The Thousand-Faced Fox gave a small nod.
“To the people of the world, that person seemed perfect in every way.”
“I know. The Martial God excelled at everything. No—he was overwhelming.”
“But he was a person too. And in the end, he succeeded. For some reason, these old eyes see the two of you overlapping.”
Mae Jonghak went still. For a while, he said nothing, gazing at the old martial artist who stood straight before him. Then he spoke.
“Great Hero Song.”
“Yes?”
“It truly is... a fine day.”
“The sky is clear.”
“May I ask the time?”
“It is the wu hour. Everyone is waiting for one person.”
“I’m late.”
“You’re not late. This is only the beginning.”
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak turned his head. Powerful sunlight poured through the wide-open window.
Yes. It truly is a fine day.
He repeated the words to himself. After taking in the blue sky, he slowly turned around.
At that moment, the Thousand-Faced Fox realized that the young man before him was no longer merely a martial artist.
“Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”
The quiet voice pierced Song Ho’s ears.
The Hidden Shadow Pavilion answered directly to the Alliance Leader’s Hall, and only one person had the authority to command its chief.
Song Ho took a deep breath and clasped his hands.
“Song Ho, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion. I await the Alliance Leader’s command.”
Mae Jonghak’s next words marked the beginning of the New Murim Alliance—and its new Alliance Leader’s first order.
“Let’s go raise the flag.”
The old martial artist’s eyelids trembled. Then he answered with a cry as strong as any young man’s.
“As you command!”
I looked up at the sky. The sun had climbed high into the blue and was pouring down fierce sunlight.
Not even a cool breeze stirred. One thought flashed through my mind.
It’s hot.
The heat was intense, but I wasn’t uncomfortably warm.
That wasn’t just because I’d become Unaffected by Cold and Heat after reaching the Supreme Peak realm.
It wasn’t the sunlight I could feel now. It was the heat rising from the crowd—the aura pouring off countless people.
Sssss.
Below the high platform, so many martial artists stood gathered that I couldn’t begin to count them. Their combined aura seemed to have stopped even the wind.
Qi rose from them like a heat haze, burning hotter and fiercer than the sunlight overhead.
Then, through that heat, the person everyone had been waiting for finally appeared.
Thud. Thud.
His firm footsteps reached every ear. The sound alone was enough to make bodies tense and minds snap to attention.
The wandering martial artist who had caused a drunken disturbance only yesterday swallowed hard. So did the orthodox and unorthodox martial artists who had gotten into a brawl with each other.
All because of one man’s presence.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak.
The One God, Three Saints, and Ten Kings.
If the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the fifteen pillars supporting the world, then the people bearing those titles were the heroes who had made that world anew.
Ten kings stood upon the earth. Above them stretched the unreachable sky of the Martial God, adorned with three stars.
And...
The brightest star of them all.
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak. The Number One Sword Under Heaven.
Shhk-shhk-shhk!
Thousands of martial artists parted at once.
No cheers or exclamations could be heard.

Some were stunned by Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s youthful appearance, while others shuddered at the overwhelming aura they could feel against their skin. But not one dared voice a question or say anything aloud.
No. They couldn’t doubt him.
This was a path meant for one person alone.
Mae Jonghak passed through the ranks and ascended the high platform. Standing there like a giant, he swept his calm gaze over the crowd.
“You’ve all been waiting a long time.”
The platform was reserved for a select few.
Sect Leaders of prestigious great sects, Family Heads of great families, and heroes and masters who had earned great fame regardless of their origins. They were the people who belonged here.
Jeok Cheongang, the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I are among them.
But if those on the platform were the pillars of the new Murim Alliance, Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was its foundation and its head.
Without anyone taking the lead, we all rose from our seats and clasped our hands toward him.
Dozens of us spoke at once, our voices so perfectly matched they sounded like one.
“We greet the Alliance Leader.”
Everyone paid their respects with solemn faces—even Jeok Cheongang and Cheongpung, seated on either side of me.
Mae Jonghak gave us a faint smile, nodded, and turned away.
The next moment, every martial artist below—thousands of them, perhaps even ten thousand—heard his voice clearly.
It shook heaven and earth.
“Peace is over.”
The air surrounding us burst apart.
A towering tree trembled, and the heroes gathered below the platform froze like statues.
Mae Jonghak continued, his words carrying an extraordinary force of internal energy. Nothing remained of the eccentric man I’d known until now.
“War has already begun. Another hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path are approaching the Central Plains.”
Some in the crowd had never lived through the Great Faction War, but none were ignorant of its horrors.
Fear and anger filled the eyes of the older martial artists. The younger ones trembled at a feeling they could not name.
“Dharma King Hong Dao.”
At Mae Jonghak’s next words, the monks of Shaolin softly murmured Buddhist invocations.
“Poison King Tang Taesang. And the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun of Emei.”
Tang Sadok, the Myriad-Poison Asura, had made the long journey despite his ailing body. His green eyes gleamed, while the nuns of Emei Sect wept.
“The bloodshed that began in Shanxi Province spread to Henan, then reached Sichuan and Hubei.”
Countless lives had been lost in little more than a year.
Old martial artists praised by all and young greenhorns alike had fallen before their lives could fully bloom.
Eight Spring Gorge.
I could still see it whenever I closed my eyes.
How many people had died in that narrow gorge in Shanxi Province?
Who had fallen in Henan, Sichuan, and Hubei?
I didn’t know their names or the dreams they’d held while they were alive.
But I knew why they had taken up their swords.
To protect something precious.
Boom!
An unprecedented aura burst from Mae Jonghak’s entire body.
Purple qi rooted in the Zaha Divine Technique rolled over his shoulders like waves.
“Take up your weapons and fight back.”
His manner of speaking and his aura weren’t the only things that had changed.
Right now, before he was the Sword Saint or the Number One Sword Under Heaven, Mae Jonghak was the Alliance Leader guiding us all.
“For the sake of the families who share our blood. For the sake of the Senior Brothers and fellow disciples, and the sects with which we have shared joy and hardship. And...”
A mighty shout erupted from his lips.
“To protect the Murim in which we live, take up your weapons!”
The giant roared. A shiver ran up my spine.
The martial artists filling the grounds let out the breaths they’d been holding and raised a thunderous cheer.
“Waaaaaah!”
“For the destruction of the Demonic Path!”
Shhk, chakachachang!
The world flooded with light. Countless weapons flashed in the sunlight pouring down overhead.
“Waaaaaah!”
“For justice and chivalry!”
Shhk, chakachachang!
The world flooded with light. Countless weapons flashed in the sunlight pouring down overhead.
Mae Jonghak gazed at the dazzling, magnificent sight, then grasped the enormous flag lying at his feet.
Murim Alliance.
Those three characters had been written across it in bold, flowing strokes. Once he raised the flag, a new era would begin.
But what he did next caught everyone by surprise.
“Great Hero Jeok. Would you help me?”
I could feel the crowd’s agitation against my skin. Jeok Cheongang, who had been silently staring at Mae Jonghak, suddenly spoke.
“Is the flag heavy?”
“It seems to be, for now.”
“That flag feels heavy even to this old man. And the more hands, the better.”
I knew what I had to do.
At Jeok Cheongang’s signal, Cheongpung and I stepped forward and took hold of the flag together.
Then we pulled it upright with all our strength.
The Murim Alliance had been born.

sentences.text: The Alliance Leader’s Hall was silent.
Only one person remained where countless people had come and gone just one shichen—approximately two hours—earlier.
“How quickly the years pass.”
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak murmured the words under his breath.
His youthful face was turned toward empty space, but his gaze was searching a distant past.
Few people alive still shared those old memories.
They’re all gone now.
Of those who shared Mae Jonghak’s memories, very few had lived out their natural spans.
Most had fallen in nameless wastelands and fields, never to rise again.
The monster known as the Great Faction War had claimed countless lives and turned the survivors into heroes.
But in the end... here we are again.
Enough time had passed for the mountains and rivers to change four times over.
Peace had come to the world.
The pain and sorrow of war had faded, and orthodox Murim had sung of the glory of victory.
Then a dark cloud called Dark Heaven appeared in a sky that had seemed destined to remain blue forever.
Peace is over.
The runny-nosed child who had not understood the horrors of war had become middle-aged, while the young man who had drawn his weapon and burned with righteous indignation had grown old.
Those who had not even been born back then had come to Henan seeking glory rather than justice.
Their lives, personalities, and goals were all different.
And Sword Saint Mae Jonghak knew it well.
He—and no one else—would have to lead them all into battle once again.
He would have to defeat Dark Heaven, which sought to plunge the world into misery.
That was when a low voice slipped between Mae Jonghak’s firmly closed lips.
“Every now and then, I wonder whether I can truly do it.”
He was not talking to himself.
Mae Jonghak knew it, and so did the person who had been quietly standing guard by the door.
Thousand-Faced Fox Song Ho, a sturdy old man, stepped forward as he answered.
“You can.”
Clack.
The tip of his prosthetic leg struck the floor, the sound echoing unusually loudly.
Beneath his hanging white hair, his shrewd eyes shone with force.
“No—you must.”
“I know.”
Mae Jonghak let out a quiet sigh.
“But I’ve known nothing but the sword my entire life.
That’s how I came by the empty title of Sword Saint.”
“It’s precisely because you are the Sword Saint that everyone will trust and follow you.”
“Being a martial artist is different from being a leader.
I never even became the Sect Leader of a single faction.”
“It’s not that you couldn’t.
You chose not to.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox was right.
When the Great Faction War ended and Huashan’s former Sect Leader passed away, every disciple of Huashan had been certain that Sword Saint Mae Jonghak would become their new Sect Leader.
“But you refused.
In the end, the Sect Leader’s Command Token went to your Disciple, Heavenly Sword True Person.”
“It was only natural.
He was more suited to becoming Huashan’s Sect Leader than I was.
And...”
Mae Jonghak ran his fingers over the treasured sword at his waist before continuing.
“I simply liked the sword.”
The Thousand-Faced Fox gazed quietly at Mae Jonghak, then suddenly spoke.
“I don’t know if I ever told you this.”
“Told me what?”
“That person once struggled with the same concern.”
“If you mean that person... surely you’re talking about the Martial God?”
The Thousand-Faced Fox gave a small nod.
“To the people of the world, that person seemed perfect in every way.”
“I know.
The Martial God excelled at everything.
No—he was overwhelming.”
“But he was a person too.
And in the end, he succeeded.
For some reason, these old eyes see the two of you overlapping.”
Mae Jonghak went still.
For a while, he said nothing, gazing at the old martial artist who stood straight before him.
Then he spoke.
“Great Hero Song.”
“Yes?”
“It truly is... a fine day.”
“The sky is clear.”
“May I ask the time?”
“It is the wu hour.
Everyone is waiting for one person.”
“I’m late.”
“You’re not late.
This is only the beginning.”
Sword Saint Mae Jonghak turned his head.
Powerful sunlight poured through the wide-open window.
Yes.
It truly is a fine day.
He repeated the words to himself.
After taking in the blue sky, he slowly turned around.
At that moment, the Thousand-Faced Fox realized that the young man before him was no longer merely a martial artist.
“Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.”
The quiet voice pierced Song Ho’s ears.
The Hidden Shadow Pavilion answered directly to the Alliance Leader’s Hall, and only one person had the authority to command its chief.
Song Ho took a deep breath and clasped his hands.
“Song Ho, Chief of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion.
I await the Alliance Leader’s command.”
Mae Jonghak’s next words marked the beginning of the New Murim Alliance—and its new Alliance Leader’s first order.
“Let’s go raise the flag.”
The old martial artist’s eyelids trembled.
Then he answered with a cry as strong as any young man’s.
“As you command!”
I looked up at the sky.
The sun had climbed high into the blue and was pouring down fierce sunlight.
Not even a cool breeze stirred.
One thought flashed through my mind.
It’s hot.
The heat was intense, but I wasn’t uncomfortably warm.
That wasn’t just because I’d become Unaffected by Cold and Heat after reaching the Supreme Peak realm.
It wasn’t the sunlight I could feel now.

Sssss.

chapters.title: Chapter 526
paragraphs: “Waaaaaaah!”
Boom! Boom! Boom!
A thunderous roar swallowed everything.
Thousands of martial artists shouted with internal energy behind their voices. Their fierce fighting spirit roused tranquil Mount Song, and their cries echoed without end.
A flag flew high above them. Each had a different name, a different nature, a different life. They were men and women from every walk of life, but now they stood beneath the same banner.
Murim Alliance.
Those three words were all that had been written across the pure white cloth.
The flag was neither as splendid as an emperor’s nor as enormous as the Demonic Cult’s standard had been when its army invaded the Central Plains.
But it was enough.
Everything was contained within those three words: Murim Alliance.
Now the martial artists of the Central Plains would become one beneath that flag. In the new era they had opened for themselves, they would fight a new enemy.
And...
“A new hero will be born.”
The quiet mutter came from somewhere.
From atop a towering tree now thick with leaves, Mungyeong watched the scene below. His gaze came to rest on one person.
Jin Taekyung.
Mungyeong could see the fire in the young man’s eyes as he stood like an iron tower, holding the flag.
With two giants—the Sword Saint and the Fire King—and another rising star, Huashan Divine Dragon Cheongpung, beside him, Taekyung received the cheers raining down from every direction.
He already looked every bit a hero.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon!”
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung!”
The martial artists chanted the name of the young hero holding the Murim Alliance’s flag.
As Mungyeong watched, another quiet murmur escaped him.
“It’s finally beginning.”
A new era. A new enemy. And new heroes.
At last, the curtain had risen on a stage long closed.
Some would fall on nameless fields and never rise again. Others would carve their names into a page of Murim’s long history.
Life and death. Humiliation and glory.
Right here, on Mount Song, the prelude to a massive war for the world was beginning.
The world trembled. No—it was undergoing a tremendous upheaval.
Until something happened, it was only rumor, no more real than fiction. But once it became reality, its impact was enormous.
The Mount Song Resolution.
On a warm spring day, news spread far and wide that the Nine Sects and One Gang, the Five Great Families, and countless other Murim factions had finally gathered beneath a single flag.
It meant that a fierce war to decide who would rule the world had begun.
“Sect Leader, they say the Murim Alliance has been founded in Henan!”
“Send a messenger pigeon immediately. Our sect will gladly stand beneath the Murim Alliance’s flag.”
“Yes, Sect Leader!”
“Send word to the other Sect Leaders in Fujian as well. We need to meet.”
The world was vast, with more sects and families than anyone could count.
Those who had been unable to make the journey to Henan for one reason or another declared their intention to join the Murim Alliance. Martial artists without a sect chose their own paths.
“Great Hero Jang, come to Henan with me. Shouldn’t we join the Murim Alliance?”
“I’m sorry, but I intend to go to Sichuan. You’ll have to travel to Henan without me, Great Hero Gwak.”
“Huh. Qingcheng and Emei may still stand, but if Dark Heaven heads to Sichuan first, as the Demonic Cult once did, the region could become a demon-slaying battleground.”
“That is precisely why I must go to Sichuan. Shouldn’t I lend whatever aid I can?”
Some carried the words righteous chivalry in their hearts.
“Brother, it sounds as though we’re headed the same way. Let’s travel together.”
“You’re a true hero. May I ask your name?”

“My name? Never mind that. I’m just a wandering martial artist who makes his living by the sword, so spare me that embarrassing ‘hero’ business. I don’t know how strong these Dark Heaven bastards are, but if I kill enough of them, I’ll make a name for myself and earn a decent sum.”
Others took up their weapons, driven by competitive spirit and dreams of making a name for themselves.
Among those who belonged to no particular sect and set out for their own reasons were unfamiliar faces—people who had not appeared in Murim for years, or had never appeared at all.
“What brings you out here, Master?”
“The weather was pleasant, so I came out for some air. But you look troubled. What happened?”
“Well, I was wandering through the mountains looking for snow ginseng to give you, Master, when I met a herb gatherer. He told me that...”
Rumors that the Murim Alliance would be restored in Henan had spread well before the Mount Song Resolution.
News of Murim’s affairs reached even the reclusive masters who had withdrawn from the world into remote mountains and deep valleys.
“Hmm. Dark Heaven and the Murim Alliance...”
“They say everything below the mountain is in an uproar. The Murim Alliance has declared war on Dark Heaven, and the common people are trembling with fear.”
“Hah. After a long peace, calamity has come.”
“Master, what should we do?”
“Countless people will die, as they did during the Great Faction War. Prepare at once, before it’s too late. We’re going to Henan.”
An old master who had spent his remaining years in a nameless valley set out for the Central Plains with his Disciple.
“Old Master, did you catch much today?”
“Bah. The fish aren’t biting worth a damn.”
“Haha. You’ve been saying that for forty years. I caught a few carp. Take some home to eat.”
“Of course I will. I saved your father’s life ten years ago, didn’t I? Give me a big, plump one.”
“All right. Since this is the last time, take them all.”
“Hmm? The last time? What kind of nonsense is that?”
“Haven’t you heard? They say a great calamity has come to Murim.”
“A calamity? Tell me more.”

“They say something called the Murim Alliance has been formed in Henan, and that it’s going to fight Dark Heaven, which is said to be the successor to that Demonic Cult. No one knows what might happen, so I was going to take my family and leave for a while... Old Master? What are you doing?”
“Can’t you see? I’m getting ready to leave.”
“Where are you going? Wait, you’re leaving your fishing rod?”
“I don’t think I’ll need it anymore. You keep it.”
“Old Master! Old Master!”
“We’ll meet again someday. Stay safe.”
The white-haired old man who had spent his days beside a secluded lake departed with a spear on his back instead of a fishing rod.

Some of the old martial artists who had once dominated an era—or some of the reclusive masters from remote valleys who had devoted their entire lives to the single character martial—stepped back into the secular world and flowed into the wider world.
“Is this the Murim Alliance?”
“It is. But if you’ve come to join, we can’t let you in right away. You’ll need to go to that pavilion and provide your sobriquet, your name, and something to prove your identity...”
“Then I’ve come to the right place. Go tell them Hong Jeok is here.”
“Hong Jeok, Red Turbans, whatever you call yourself, you still have to go through verification... Wait. What did you just say?”
“Hong Jeok. Hong Jeok of Guangxi.”
“Th-the Fist King...!”
Names swept away by the waves of time, sobriquets that had vanished from sight.
And yet, despite everything, titles clearly etched into the memories of ordinary people began appearing everywhere.
Even when the sun set and darkness fell, their presence shone like torches.
And rumors of the newly risen stars continued to pass from mouth to mouth.
“I’ll guarantee the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes will play a major role in this war.”
At the middle-aged man’s words, the narrow-eyed man snorted. The speaker had a chin shaped like a spatula.
“What a joke. Call them the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes or the finest young prodigies in the martial world, but weren’t they picked from the disciples and heirs of prestigious sects and families?”
“And? What’s your point?”
“They’re hothouse flowers. How much good will people raised in comfort be on a battlefield?”
Spatula Chin narrowed his eyes.
“Listen to this fellow. Are you with Dark Heaven?”
“What!”
Bird Eyes bristled and shouted.
“They say even a crooked mouth ought to speak straight. Don’t say something that could get me killed! Why would I be with Dark Heaven?”
“Then why are you putting down the pillars of our orthodox faction?”
“Putting them down? I’m just stating the facts! It’s not as though I can shave down your chin!”
“What does my chin have to do with this? Why are you insulting my looks?”
Fire blazed in Spatula Chin’s eyes.
“Say one more word about my chin and you’ll regret it. Got that?”
“Spatula Chin! That chin takes my breath away! Chin-chin, ka-thunk-thunk-chin!”
“You fucking bastard!”
Crash! Crack!
The table overturned, sending side dishes and liquor bottles tumbling to the floor.
A sword fight seemed ready to break out at any moment. Watching Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin square off, a man with a goatee spoke with measured dignity.
“You’re both wrong.”
Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin turned toward him together.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“I’ll rip out every hair of that beard.”
The goateed man shook his head and continued.
“I don’t doubt the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes will distinguish themselves. But compared with the strength Dark Heaven has shown so far, they’re still only young prodigies.”
Bird Eyes brightened.
“So I’m right?”
“To a degree.”
“I knew it. You’ve got uncommon insight. Your beard looks especially fine today.”
Spatula Chin ground his teeth and glared at Bird Eyes.
“Your eyes are smaller than your asshole, and now you’re deaf too? Did you already forget he said both of us were wrong?”
“...Fair point. But why? I don’t see what’s wrong with what I said.”
The goateed man stroked his beard as he answered.

“There are genuine talents everywhere. You’re right that the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes grew up in the best possible conditions. But that doesn’t change the fact that they’re the finest young prodigies in the martial world.”
“Hm. And?”
“Nor are they all disciples of prestigious sects. Jin Mukyung, the Heaven Shaking Sword and Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, is a prime example.”
“Ah, I forgot about the Heaven Shaking Sword.”
Spatula Chin, who had been waiting for an opening, cut in with a mocking grin.
“The Heaven Shaking Sword is impressive, but Murong Yeonghwi, a blood relative of the Murong Family, is overwhelming too. Still, what could a nobody like you possibly know?”
“What did you say, you bastard? If you fell in the water, that chin would float...”
The two began growling at each other again. The goateed man sighed deeply.
“Stop fighting and listen. The young prodigies to watch aren’t the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes. The Two Dragons stand above them.”
Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin froze.
Even they had to admit he was right. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes could not compare with those two Divine Dragons: Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung and Huashan Divine Dragon Cheongpung.
“Certainly...”
“That’s true.”
They nodded despite themselves. Then a question occurred to them.
“What are those two doing right now?”
“Who knows? But one thing is certain.”
The goateed man continued, his expression solemn.
“They must be doing something extraordinary.”
Cheongpung spoke with a stiff expression.
“Ahh, I want dumplings!”
Don’t say it so loudly, you idiot.

Some would fall on nameless fields and never rise again.
Others would carve their names into a page of Murim’s long history.
Life and death.
Humiliation and glory.
Right here, on Mount Song, the prelude to a massive war for the world was beginning.
The world trembled.
No—it was undergoing a tremendous upheaval.
Until something happened, it was only rumor, no more real than fiction.
But once it became reality, its impact was enormous.
The Mount Song Resolution.
On a warm spring day, news spread far and wide that the Nine Sects and One Gang, the Five Great Families, and countless other Murim factions had finally gathered beneath a single flag.
It meant that a fierce war to decide who would rule the world had begun.
“Sect Leader, they say the Murim Alliance has been founded in Henan!”
“Send a messenger pigeon immediately.
Our sect will gladly stand beneath the Murim Alliance’s flag.”
“Yes, Sect Leader!”
“Send word to the other Sect Leaders in Fujian as well.
We need to meet.”
The world was vast, with more sects and families than anyone could count.
Those who had been unable to make the journey to Henan for one reason or another declared their intention to join the Murim Alliance.
Martial artists without a sect chose their own paths.
“Great Hero Jang, come to Henan with me.
Shouldn’t we join the Murim Alliance?”
“I’m sorry, but I intend to go to Sichuan.
You’ll have to travel to Henan without me, Great Hero Gwak.”
“Huh.
Qingcheng and Emei may still stand, but if Dark Heaven heads to Sichuan first, as the Demonic Cult once did, the region could become a demon-slaying battleground.”
“That is precisely why I must go to Sichuan.
Shouldn’t I lend whatever aid I can?”
Some carried the words righteous chivalry in their hearts.
“Brother, it sounds as though we’re headed the same way.
Let’s travel together.”
“You’re a true hero.
May I ask your name?”
“My name?
Never mind that.
I’m just a wandering martial artist who makes his living by the sword, so spare me that embarrassing ‘hero’ business.
I don’t know how strong these Dark Heaven bastards are, but if I kill enough of them, I’ll make a name for myself and earn a decent sum.”
Others took up their weapons, driven by competitive spirit and dreams of making a name for themselves.
Among those who belonged to no particular sect and set out for their own reasons were unfamiliar faces—people who had not appeared in Murim for years, or had never appeared at all.
“What brings you out here, Master?”
“The weather was pleasant, so I came out for some air.
But you look troubled.
What happened?”
“Well, I was wandering through the mountains looking for snow ginseng to give you, Master, when I met a herb gatherer.
He told me that...”
Rumors that the Murim Alliance would be restored in Henan had spread well before the Mount Song Resolution.
News of Murim’s affairs reached even the reclusive masters who had withdrawn from the world into remote mountains and deep valleys.
“Hmm.
Dark Heaven and the Murim Alliance...”
“They say everything below the mountain is in an uproar.
The Murim Alliance has declared war on Dark Heaven, and the common people are trembling with fear.”
“Hah.
After a long peace, calamity has come.”
“Master, what should we do?”
“Countless people will die, as they did during the Great Faction War.
Prepare at once, before it’s too late.
We’re going to Henan.”
An old master who had spent his remaining years in a nameless valley set out for the Central Plains with his Disciple.
“Old Master, did you catch much today?”
“Bah.
The fish aren’t biting worth a damn.”
“Haha.
You’ve been saying that for forty years.
I caught a few carp.
Take some home to eat.”
“Of course I will.
I saved your father’s life ten years ago, didn’t I?
Give me a big, plump one.”
“All right.
Since this is the last time, take them all.”
“Hmm?
The last time?
What kind of nonsense is that?”
“Haven’t you heard?
They say a great calamity has come to Murim.”
“A calamity?
Tell me more.”
“They say something called the Murim Alliance has been formed in Henan, and that it’s going to fight Dark Heaven, which is said to be the successor to that Demonic Cult.
No one knows what might happen, so I was going to take my family and leave for a while...
Old Master?
What are you doing?”
“Can’t you see?
I’m getting ready to leave.”
“Where are you going?
Wait, you’re leaving your fishing rod?”
“I don’t think I’ll need it anymore.
You keep it.”
“Old Master!
Old Master!”
“We’ll meet again someday.
Stay safe.”
The white-haired old man who had spent his days beside a secluded lake departed with a spear on his back instead of a fishing rod.

Some of the old martial artists who had once dominated an era—or some of the reclusive masters from remote valleys who had devoted their entire lives to the single character martial—stepped back into the secular world and flowed into the wider world.
“Is this the Murim Alliance?”
“It is.
But if you’ve come to join, we can’t let you in right away.
You’ll need to go to that pavilion and provide your sobriquet, your name, and something to prove your identity...”
“Then I’ve come to the right place.
Go tell them Hong Jeok is here.”
“Hong Jeok, Red Turbans, whatever you call yourself, you still have to go through verification...
Wait.
What did you just say?”
“Hong Jeok.
Hong Jeok of Guangxi.”
“Th-the Fist King...!”
Names swept away by the waves of time, sobriquets that had vanished from sight.
And yet, despite everything, titles clearly etched into the memories of ordinary people began appearing everywhere.
Even when the sun set and darkness fell, their presence shone like torches.
And rumors of the newly risen stars continued to pass from mouth to mouth.
“I’ll guarantee the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes will play a major role in this war.”
At the middle-aged man’s words, the narrow-eyed man snorted.
The speaker had a chin shaped like a spatula.
“What a joke.
Call them the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes or the finest young prodigies in the martial world, but weren’t they picked from the disciples and heirs of prestigious sects and families?”
“And?
What’s your point?”
“They’re hothouse flowers.
How much good will people raised in comfort be on a battlefield?”
Spatula Chin narrowed his eyes.
“Listen to this fellow.
Are you with Dark Heaven?”
“What!”
Bird Eyes bristled and shouted.
“They say even a crooked mouth ought to speak straight.
Don’t say something that could get me killed!
Why would I be with Dark Heaven?”
“Then why are you putting down the pillars of our orthodox faction?”
“Putting them down?
I’m just stating the facts!
It’s not as though I can shave down your chin!”
“What does my chin have to do with this?
Why are you insulting my looks?”
Fire blazed in Spatula Chin’s eyes.
“Say one more word about my chin and you’ll regret it.
Got that?”
“Spatula Chin!
That chin takes my breath away!
Chin-chin, ka-thunk-thunk-chin!”
“You fucking bastard!”
Crash!
Crack!
The table overturned, sending side dishes and liquor bottles tumbling to the floor.
A sword fight seemed ready to break out at any moment.
Watching Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin square off, a man with a goatee spoke with measured dignity.
“You’re both wrong.”
Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin turned toward him together.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“I’ll rip out every hair of that beard.”
The goateed man shook his head and continued.
“I don’t doubt the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes will distinguish themselves.
But compared with the strength Dark Heaven has shown so far, they’re still only young prodigies.”
Bird Eyes brightened.
“So I’m right?”
“To a degree.”
“I knew it.
You’ve got uncommon insight.
Your beard looks especially fine today.”
Spatula Chin ground his teeth and glared at Bird Eyes.
“Your eyes are smaller than your asshole, and now you’re deaf too?
Did you already forget he said both of us were wrong?”
“...Fair point.
But why?
I don’t see what’s wrong with what I said.”
The goateed man stroked his beard as he answered.
“There are genuine talents everywhere.
You’re right that the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes grew up in the best possible conditions.
But that doesn’t change the fact that they’re the finest young prodigies in the martial world.”
“Hm.
And?”
“Nor are they all disciples of prestigious sects.
Jin Mukyung, the Heaven Shaking Sword and Second Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, is a prime example.”
“Ah, I forgot about the Heaven Shaking Sword.”
Spatula Chin, who had been waiting for an opening, cut in with a mocking grin.
“The Heaven Shaking Sword is impressive, but Murong Yeonghwi, a blood relative of the Murong Family, is overwhelming too.
Still, what could a nobody like you possibly know?”
“What did you say, you bastard?
If you fell in the water, that chin would float...”
The two began growling at each other again.
The goateed man sighed deeply.
“Stop fighting and listen.
The young prodigies to watch aren’t the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
The Two Dragons stand above them.”
Bird Eyes and Spatula Chin froze.
Even they had to admit he was right.
The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes could not compare with those two Divine Dragons: Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung and Huashan Divine Dragon Cheongpung.
“Certainly...”
“That’s true.”
They nodded despite themselves.
Then a question occurred to them.
“What are those two doing right now?”
“Who knows?
But one thing is certain.”
The goateed man continued, his expression solemn.
“They must be doing something extraordinary.”
Cheongpung spoke with a stiff expression.
“Ahh, I want dumplings!”
Don’t say it so loudly, you idiot.

chapters.title: Chapter 527
paragraphs: Seven days and nights had passed since the day people called the Mount Song Resolution.

Amid the shouts of countless Murim heroes, the Murim Alliance’s flag had been raised once more. News that the Alliance had officially been restored for the first time in decades swept beyond Henan and shook the entire Murim world.
Things have been moving at a frantic pace.
At first, I’d thought there was no reason for me to be particularly busy. I learned how naïve that was less than half a day after the Murim Alliance was formed.
“Captain. I hear there’s a visitor downstairs.”
“What do you mean, you hear there’s a visitor?”
“Apparently Cheongpung ran into him on his way back from buying dumplings. He says the man’s waiting downstairs.”
“I suddenly want dumplings. And I’m not meeting him.”
“I caught a glimpse of him. He looked like someone important.”
“What, am I some lowborn bastard? Send our important guest home with all due courtesy.”
“How could I do that? I hear he made an appointment.”
“What the hell are you talking about? I haven’t made any appointments since I got here. And how many people do I even know?”
“That’s true. You don’t have any friends, Captain.”
“Really? Because it looks like you’re about to lose your head.”
“Hmm. Maybe he spoke with the Lesser Family Head?”
“This bastard doesn’t even flinch anymore.”
“Spend three years as Hyuk Mujin, and you wind up with about three lives.”
“Enough nonsense. Send him back. Ah, but who exactly is this important person?”
“Oh, wait a moment. I’ll go ask.”
“Go on.”
Hyuk Mujin went downstairs at a leisurely pace, then came racing back.
“K-K-Kongtong Sect! The Kongtong Sect Leader!”
“Bring him in at once! Bring him innnn!”
Wait, why is hyung here?
Starting with the Sect Leader of the Kongtong Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, a steady stream of renowned figures of Murim came to visit.

The Family Head of the Namgung Family, whom I already knew, came in person. People from sects and families I’d formed connections with while traveling across the Murim world arrived one after another.
Of course, far more of them came to make a new connection.
“Captain.”
“...Who is it this time?”
“The Shandong Yue Family. The Family Head came in person.”
“...Receive him with due courtesy.”
“A representative from the Murim world of Guizhou was sent as well...”
“...Bring him in as well.”
“Oh, and Captain.”
“...Bring him in.”
I hadn’t realized I was this famous. No, to be precise, I hadn’t realized I was this famous.
After three days of meeting one visitor after another, I was exhausted.
Fuck, I can’t keep doing this.
It would be one thing if these were blind dates with pretty women.

But dealing with more than ten middle-aged and old men every day left me feeling like my soul had been sucked out. By then, the smell of tea alone made me nauseous, and the conversations across those teacups were mostly the same.
“Oh! So you’re the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon I’ve heard so much about!”
The Jin Taekyung Conversation Guide.
Had they all read a book with that title before coming? Every one of them opened with the same line.
But even an obedient child eventually gets contrary. At first, I’d forced a smile and exchanged meaningless pleasantries. As time went on, I got more honest.
“I’ve heard many rumors about you.”
“I’ve heard plenty of stories about myself too.”
“A young hero has appeared in Murim. It’s truly wonderful. Ho ho ho.”
“I’m the happiest person of all. Ha ha ha.”
“Incidentally, I have a daughter of marriageable age...”
“I have two older brothers of marriageable age.”
“Good heavens, man! How dare you spring your daughter on him out of nowhere? Have you lost your mind? Young Hero Jin, don’t pay that fellow any mind.”
“It’s all right. I wasn’t listening anyway.”
“Then listen to me instead.”
“Wow. So that’s where this is going.”
“As a matter of fact, I have a daughter too. I’m sure you’ll like her.”
“I’ll stake Hyuk Mujin’s balls that I won’t.”
“What are you talking about? Balls—no, what man in the world would turn down a beauty?”
“A beauty? Is your daughter very pretty?”
“Do you even have to ask? Her beauty is already famous throughout Fujian!”
“Oh. Ohhh.”
“Everyone knows her! Stop anyone passing by and ask. She’s already pretty, but in five years, she’ll surely be the First Beauty of Fujian!”
“Ohhh, the First Beauty of Fujian... Wait. Why five years?”
“She’s twelve.”
“Get out.”
I could hardly remember how those seven days and nights had passed.
Some of my visitors already knew me, while others came out of simple curiosity. Most, though, wanted to forge some kind of connection with me or the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
And not all of them were martial artists.
“Captain. Someone from a place called Central Plains Commerce is asking to see you.”
“Bring them in—no, wait. Why is a trading company looking for me? My eldest brother, maybe, but me?”
“I’m not sure why. But I have an eye for people, and they don’t seem bad. It might be worth meeting them.”
“Hey.”
“Y-Yes?”
“You bastard. Central Plains Commerce slipped you money, didn’t they?”
“Gasp! H-How did you know?”
“Give back every last bit and send them away. While I’m still asking nicely.”
Now there were even people slipping bribes to Hyuk Mujin.

Most of the visitors so far had arranged their appointments through Jin Wikyung, so I’d met them reluctantly. They knew full well he was the only way to get an appointment with me. Anyone who came directly fell into one of two categories.
Either Jin Wikyung would turn them away for some disqualifying reason, or their standing was so high they could show up whenever they pleased.
The first was far more common. Those people usually tried some shallow trick, then left without so much as seeing my face.
Why were they going to such lengths? I had a pretty good idea why all this attention had suddenly fallen on me.
The flag, obviously.
On the day the Murim Alliance was officially proclaimed, I’d raised its flag together with Mae Jonghak, the new Alliance Leader, Jeok Cheongang, and Cheongpung.
It had moved me, but I hadn’t thought much more of it. To everyone else who’d witnessed it, apparently, it had been an enormous culture shock.
I suppose it makes sense. Two young punks got the spotlight instead of all those elders.
The platform had been packed with people from prestigious sects and families, including the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.

Murim had reached such an extreme level of population aging that the platform could have passed for a senior center. Even the men in their forties who’d managed to get up there were little more than pu’er tea runners. Yet Cheongpung and I, barely past twenty, had the audacity to take part in that glorious, historic moment.
The sight had clearly startled everyone. Some nodded, acknowledging the ability and qualifications of those two young punks. Others seemed to find it deeply irritating.
The Zhongnan Sect, for example.

I couldn’t be sure, but their guts were probably twisted with resentment by now. After all, the Jin Family of Taiyuan and I had begun rising rapidly, and our history with them was anything but friendly.

The bad blood had started with the Three Hands of Zhongnan, the three idiots of the Zhongnan Sect. It had worsened when the Roaring Fury Swordsman came to the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s New Year’s Day banquet and caused a scene, only to be beaten by Jeok Cheongang like a dog on the hottest day of summer.

And that wasn’t all. The feud had reached its peak when the Taeeul Merciless Sword, regarded alongside the Sect Leader Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord as the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest master, was defeated by me.

After that much humiliation, seeing me in the spotlight must have made them grind their teeth. For all I knew, they were somewhere right now biting, tearing, and chewing on me, the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and Jeok Cheongang.
Given the personalities of the Zhongnan Sect’s people I had seen so far, I could almost believe it if they joined hands with Dark Heaven.
Hey, Zhongnan Sect.
Dark Heaven! Come on in.
The Murim Alliance has been formed. Why the long faces?
Jin Taekyung is pissing us off. That fucking brat.
Ho ho ho. Want a hit of a Temporary Strength Pill?
Sure. Roll me one.
I could picture it. I really could.

Still, Zhongnan was a venerable orthodox sect and one of the Nine Sects and One Gang. Surely they weren’t crazy enough to join hands with Dark Heaven. But they’d find some way to get in our way at every turn.
Hang on. This isn’t fair. Why is everyone swarming me?
At the thought, I looked toward the rice weevil—or rather, the dumpling grub—fidgeting in a corner with Mimi-chan.
“Why, Benefactor?”
“Good heavens, the bug talks.”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing. But Cheongpung, why do you look so free? Doesn’t anyone come to see you?”
“I don’t meet people when I’m full. And I don’t meet them if they don’t bring me something tasty.”
I thought about that for a moment, then asked, “Aren’t you always full?”
“Yes. So I don’t meet anyone.”
“...Right.”
Must be nice not having a care in the world.
If I had to pick the person in all Murim who gave the fewest fucks and did exactly as he pleased, Cheongpung would be a strong contender.
Even on the day of the Mount Song Resolution, he’d bounced around in delight because it was his first time raising the Murim Alliance’s flag.
Is he a genius or a lunatic?
Probably both. Hmm.
As I was thinking that, Cheongpung yawned and spoke.
“And I’m not free. I’m training right now.”
“What fresh bullshit is this?”
“I’m serious. Look.”
Cheongpung took Mimi, the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, off his shoulder and began squirming in his seat.
“...Sorry to interrupt, but are you evolving into a bug?”
“No. It’s martial arts.”
“Martial arts?”
“Yes. I made it after watching Mimi move.”
Then why did it look nothing like martial arts?
I asked with complete sincerity.
“Please tell me this martial art isn’t called Squirming. Or Toughening Up. Something like that.”
“No. It’s a footwork technique.”
“...Then you should stand up and do it, you idiot.”
“Oh, right. I forgot.”
Did I really have to tell him that?
While I was at a loss for words, Cheongpung sprang to his feet and took a step.
Or rather, the moment I felt him take a step, his figure disappeared.
Whoosh!
With a faint sound, Cheongpung reached the far end of the spacious room and flashed me a toothy grin.
“Ta-da. What do you think?”
What did I just see?
Goose bumps shot up my back.
His movement was ghostlike—no, snakelike. It was unmistakably a footwork technique, and yet it wasn’t.
Cheongpung hadn’t walked. He’d slid, so fast that even I could barely follow him with my eyes.
“I mixed Mimi’s movements with a few different martial arts. Moving like this makes me feel like I’m Mimi too, and I like it!”
“...You mixed them?”
“Yes! It’s called Mimi Step! Would you like to learn it, Benefactor?”
He really is insane. In more ways than one.
I stared at Cheongpung with my mouth hanging open, then shook my head.
“No. I don’t want to.”
Just as Cheongpung’s shoulders drooped, Hyuk Mujin’s voice came from outside the door.
“Captain. There’s a visitor here.”
A visitor? Was there anyone else left who could come see me?

Jin Taekyung is pissing us off.
That fucking brat.
Ho ho ho.
Want a hit of a Temporary Strength Pill?
Sure.
Roll me one.
I could picture it.
I really could.
Still, Zhongnan was a venerable orthodox sect and one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Surely they weren’t crazy enough to join hands with Dark Heaven.
But they’d find some way to get in our way at every turn.
Hang on.
This isn’t fair.
Why is everyone swarming me?
At the thought, I looked toward the rice weevil—or rather, the dumpling grub—fidgeting in a corner with Mimi-chan.
“Why, Benefactor?”
“Good heavens, the bug talks.”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing.
But Cheongpung, why do you look so free?
Doesn’t anyone come to see you?”
“I don’t meet people when I’m full.
And I don’t meet them if they don’t bring me something tasty.”
I thought about that for a moment, then asked, “Aren’t you always full?”
“Yes.
So I don’t meet anyone.”
“...Right.”
Must be nice not having a care in the world.
If I had to pick the person in all Murim who gave the fewest fucks and did exactly as he pleased, Cheongpung would be a strong contender.
Even on the day of the Mount Song Resolution, he’d bounced around in delight because it was his first time raising the Murim Alliance’s flag.
Is he a genius or a lunatic?
Probably both.
Hmm.
As I was thinking that, Cheongpung yawned and spoke.
“And I’m not free.
I’m training right now.”
“What fresh bullshit is this?”
“I’m serious.
Look.”
Cheongpung took Mimi, the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, off his shoulder and began squirming in his seat.
“...Sorry to interrupt, but are you evolving into a bug?”
“No.
It’s martial arts.”
“Martial arts?”
“Yes.
I made it after watching Mimi move.”
Then why did it look nothing like martial arts?
I asked with complete sincerity.
“Please tell me this martial art isn’t called Squirming.
Or Toughening Up.
Something like that.”
“No.
It’s a footwork technique.”
“...Then you should stand up and do it, you idiot.”
“Oh, right.
I forgot.”
Did I really have to tell him that?
While I was at a loss for words, Cheongpung sprang to his feet and took a step.
Or rather, the moment I felt him take a step, his figure disappeared.
Whoosh!
With a faint sound, Cheongpung reached the far end of the spacious room and flashed me a toothy grin.
“Ta-da.
What do you think?”
What did I just see?
Goose bumps shot up my back.
His movement was ghostlike—no, snakelike.
It was unmistakably a footwork technique, and yet it wasn’t.
Cheongpung hadn’t walked.
He’d slid, so fast that even I could barely follow him with my eyes.
“I mixed Mimi’s movements with a few different martial arts.
Moving like this makes me feel like I’m Mimi too, and I like it!”
“...You mixed them?”
“Yes!
It’s called Mimi Step!
Would you like to learn it, Benefactor?”
He really is insane.
In more ways than one.
I stared at Cheongpung with my mouth hanging open, then shook my head.
“No.
I don’t want to.”
Just as Cheongpung’s shoulders drooped, Hyuk Mujin’s voice came from outside the door.
“Captain.
There’s a visitor here.”
A visitor?
Was there anyone else left who could come see me?

chapters.title: Chapter 528
paragraphs: Creak.
It didn’t take long to recognize the uninvited guest.
The moment I saw the familiar face come through the door, I spoke without hesitation.
“Hey, Hyuk Mujin. Who told you to let a beggar in?”
“Have you been—listen to this damn bastard.”
Gung Gibang, who had been grinning brightly despite his grimy face, scowled.
“I go out of my way to make time for you, and that’s how you greet me?”
“I called a beggar a beggar. What’s the problem?”
“Do you ever think about how it feels to be the beggar hearing it?”
“No. Not for a single second.”
“...You’re worse than a scorpion. One day, a hundred thousand Beggars’ Sect disciples will surround you and beat the hell out of you.”
I shrugged.
“Not likely. I’m a pretty valuable asset to the Murim Alliance.”
“I swear on my begging bowl, when the time comes, you’ll be the first one I beat senseless.”
“That’s fine too. It’ll mean the war is over.”
“You mean that?”
“Yeah. Promise.”
Gung Gibang glared at me in silence. Then his gaze softened, and a faint smile appeared on his lips.
“Damn it. The war’s barely begun, and already I want it to be over.”
“What, so you can beat me up?”
Gung Gibang gave a quiet laugh and shook his head.
“I may be destined to beg for the rest of my life, but I’m not stupid enough to think that way. No matter what, war must never happen.”
“You could distinguish yourself in battle and become a hero.”
“What would a beggar like me do with being a hero?”
“Oh.”
A wise answer to a stupid question.
I’d asked because I wanted to know what he really thought. I gave him a sincere round of applause.
Clap, clap, clap.
“What are you doing?”
“Nothing. Just thinking how our Gibang’s all grown up, having thoughts like that.”
“...What exactly do you think of me? And you’re younger than I am. How can you be so shameless?”
“If getting older made everyone mature, the world would be a much nicer place. Time passes without anyone having to work at it.”
In that sense, Gung Gibang’s thinking really was remarkably sound for someone his age in Murim.
This wasn’t the twenty-first-century modern world. This was Murim, where the primal law of the strong devouring the weak held sway.
It would be naive to think every martial artist now filling Henan had joined the Murim Alliance out of chivalry alone.
Especially the younger ones.
They were at an age when their blood ran hot.
Then again, middle-aged martial artists nearing forty weren’t much different. To them, the Great Faction War was little more than a trace of a past that had ended before they were born.
Plenty of people in the generations that had never known war were driven less by chivalry than by dreams of winning glory and becoming heroes.
That went for wandering martial artists who acted as if there were no tomorrow, and for disciples of the great sects and families too.
I get it. It’s the times we live in, and it’s how Murim works...
But however generously I tried to look at them, they still looked like fucking idiots to me.
Thank heavens more people had joined the Murim Alliance out of chivalry than for reasons like theirs.
Come to think of it, the people around me are pretty normal by comparison. Hmm.
Just then, Cheongpung slid forward like a snake and appeared right in front of Gung Gibang.
Ssss—
“Agh! What the fuck?”
“Hehe. This is the new footwork technique I made, Mimi Step. It really looks like Mimi, doesn’t it?”
“Like Mimi, my ass. It looks like a dog! Like a damn beggar!”
At Gung Gibang’s shriek, Hyuk Mujin spoke with the happiest expression in the world.
“Young Hero Cheongpung, could you do that one more time later?”
“Wow! Of course I can!”
“No, you can’t! Absolutely not! Don’t do it!”
Normal, my ass.
Put them together and it was hard to find a bigger bunch of fucking idiots.
Ah, my head hurts.
I rubbed my throbbing temple and asked the question I’d put off.
“Anyway, what are you here for?”
Gung Gibang shot Cheongpung a wary glance before answering.
“There are a few people who want to meet you and Cheongpung. I thought I’d stop by and ask, just in case.”
“Of course there are plenty of people who want to meet me.”
“...You’re obnoxious, but I can’t argue with that.”
“So who are they?”
Gung Gibang sighed.
“The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”
“The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?”
“The ones you know. Not all of them—about half.”
Well, obviously it was the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes I knew. Were there others?
The moment I heard the name, I’d made up my mind.
“No. What would I meet them for?”
“To get acquainted. It can’t hurt for young prodigies to be on good terms.”
“Can’t see how it would help, either. And young prodigies, my ass. Don’t put me in the same league as you lot.”
Gung Gibang stared at me in disbelief.
“...How can you say something that offensive with a straight face?”
“Because everyone knows it’s true.”
“Well, yes, but... Damn it. Fine. What about Cheongpung?”
Realizing he wasn’t going to get anywhere with me, Gung Gibang quickly changed targets.
Sssssss—

Cheongpung had been closely observing Mimi, the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, who had somehow turned into a giant snake while drawing everyone’s attention. Without even turning around, he answered.
“Hmm. I don’t want to go.”
“Even though they’ve laid out a lavish feast for you?”
“I ate dumplings earlier, so I’m full. I don’t think I’d go even if I were hungry.”
“You could take the food with you. Eat it when you get hungry.”
“I don’t know. I haven’t had much of an appetite lately.”
“Wh-what?”
Gung Gibang stared at him as if he’d been stabbed.
Hyuk Mujin and I were just as shocked.
What the hell? Is he really insane?
Captain, did I hear that wrong?
No. You heard him right. He said he has no appetite.
That bastard isn’t Cheongpung. He’s definitely a Dark Heaven spy.
That’s... convincing!
Hyuk Mujin and I carried on a silent conversation with our eyes.
That was how shocking Cheongpung’s announcement was.
Cheongpung, of all people, has no appetite?
It was news as astonishing as the founding of the New Murim Alliance. Yet Cheongpung didn’t so much as flinch beneath the astonished stares of everyone around him.
“Anyway, I’m fine. You go ahead, Benefactor.”
“Huh? Uh, no. I’m not going either.”
“Really? Hehe. Then I’ll get back to what I was doing. I think Mimi Step needs a few improvements.”
I had no idea why he was acting like this, but one thing seemed certain.
As time passed and the circumstances around him changed, some kind of change had begun in Cheongpung as well.
That guy...
I stared at Cheongpung in silence, then turned toward Gung Gibang.
“Anyway, you’d better get going.”
“Mm. I suppose so. We talked so long I’m late for our meeting.”
Still sneaking stunned glances at Cheongpung, Gung Gibang turned away and muttered, “They’ll be disappointed. Young Lady Ju seemed especially excited.”
“Disappointed? I’ve already met some of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes at the Star-Array Grand Banquet. I’m bound to run into the others again sooner or later—”
I broke off. The last thing Gung Gibang had said had taken over my thoughts.
“Wait. Who?”
“Huh? Who do you mean?”
“You said someone was especially excited.”
“Oh. Young Lady Ju?”
So I hadn’t misheard.
“By Young Lady Ju, do you mean...?”
“Of course I mean the Young Lady Ju you know. Young Lady Ju Hwaran of the Yongbong Escort Bureau—the Young Bureau Head, the Dagger Hidden Flower.”
A memory came back to me.
In Murim, it had been only two or three months ago, yet somehow it felt impossibly distant.
Ironically, it was also one of the clearest memories left behind by all that time.
“The moon is so bright tonight.”
Yes. The moon had been unusually bright that night.
Or perhaps the moon hadn’t been the brightest thing there. Perhaps it had been someone’s face.
I hadn’t been looking at the moon then.
“Great Hero Jin.”
“Yes, Young Lady Ju.”
“Do you think I can do it?”
I could almost hear her voice again, damp and desolate, drifting through the flower-filled garden.
What had I told her?
I thought for a moment before muttering blankly,
“...It’s all right even if you can’t.”
“What? What’s all right?”
I came back to myself.
The soft moonlight, the scent of flowers, the voice—all of it vanished. Even the face that had hovered before my eyes faded away.
I looked up to find Gung Gibang right in front of me, wearing a puzzled expression.
A small sigh escaped me.
“Gibang.”
“Mm?”
“Why are you so ugly?”
“I’m sorry, but I mean it. Actually, I don’t think I’m all that sorry. Things were going so well.”
Gung Gibang’s ugly face contorted.
“You little bastard, you’ve been doing this since—”
“Enough.”
I shook my head, cutting him off.
“Let’s go.”
“What?”
“Stop asking and let’s go meet the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes or whoever they are. Hearing about that feast made me hungry.”
“Uh, uh-huh?”
Gung Gibang forgot to be angry. He blinked at me, then nodded hurriedly.
“Uh, sure. They’ll all be glad to see you.”
I didn’t much care who would be glad.
It was just... well, how should I put it?
I just felt like seeing her after all this time.
Yes. That was all. Besides, I owed her thanks for something concerning Jeok Cheongang. I had every reason to go.
It’s only right. Anyone decent would go.
Muttering that to myself, I started walking. Gung Gibang’s shout that he was coming with me rang noisily from behind.
The three-story inn was large and lavish. Between its size and its prices, anyone without money to spare would have trouble setting foot inside—and, in practice, they didn’t.
The three men and one woman seated by a window on its top floor were hardly ordinary people themselves.
“Young Lady Ju, may I pour you a drink?”
“Now, now. The young lady doesn’t care much for alcohol. Isn’t that right, Young Lady Ju?”
The handsome men in gleaming silk martial uniforms and hero headbands had no idea what the woman before them was thinking.
When is he coming?
She no longer heard a word they were saying.
At some point, she had stopped leaning back in her chair and begun tilting toward the window instead. Her eyes kept darting between the half-open window and the stairs.
Gung Gibang made such a bold promise. Should I go out and see for myself?
And just as all those worries and thoughts began chasing one another in endless circles—
Jingle.
The bell rang as the inn door opened, and Ju Hwaran sprang to her feet.

chapters.title: Chapter 529
paragraphs: Jingle.
“Welcome!”
The inn attendant’s hearty cry followed the ring of the bell above the door.
Ju Hwaran sprang to her feet, hope rising in her chest. But disappointment quickly filled her eyes.
It wasn’t him. From up here, she couldn’t see the newcomer’s face properly, but she could tell that much.
No—if it had been him, she might have known him by his shadow alone.
It wasn’t him. It wasn’t that person.
Hwaran sighed softly and looked down at the first floor once more, reluctant to look away. Staring wouldn’t change anything, yet she couldn’t quite give up.
The men seated with her cleared their throats at the sight.
“Ahem.”
“Ahem.”
They had been watching Hwaran’s every move from the start. They weren’t foolish enough to miss what her reaction meant.
Three men sat across the table from her. Two of them exchanged a glance—but their eyes weren’t the only things communicating. Their lips barely moved as they spoke through Sound Transmission.
—Fellow Daoist Hwangbo. Who do you think Young Lady Ju is waiting for?

The question came from Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon. Handsome, clear-skinned, and dressed in spotless white, he was widely acknowledged as the Kunlun Sect’s finest young prodigy and was one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
At his Sound Transmission, the beautiful young man with a sharp nose slightly furrowed his brow.
—No idea.
—I can think of only one person. If I’m right, it’s the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Tae—
—Drop it.
Hwangbo Ak, the beautiful young man who had coldly cut him off, was the Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family and another member of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
He was in a foul mood.
To think I, Hwangbo Ak, would be treated as less than some other bastard.
It was unthinkable. For someone as full of himself as Hwangbo Ak, it was especially hard to accept.

The Hwangbo Family might not be one of the Five Great Families, but its name carried considerable weight throughout Murim. No one could deny that it was an old martial family that had ruled Shandong for generations.
And Hwangbo Ak was its Lesser Family Head.

He had the martial talent to earn a place among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, too, and the looks to stand out anywhere. A fine family, immense wealth and prestige, a handsome face—it was only natural that women flocked to him.
The trouble was that, for the first time in nearly thirty years of life, everything he had enjoyed seemed worthless.
The Dagger Hidden Flower, Ju Hwaran.
The moment he saw her, he had realized that all the beautiful women he’d met before were fireflies before the sun.
She wore no makeup, unlike the others, yet her face held a beauty he couldn’t describe. Even her plain-colored martial uniform looked more elegant than an ornate court dress.
He had fallen for her at first sight.
Why couldn’t I have met a woman like her sooner?

Hwangbo Ak gazed at Hwaran as though entranced. Every small movement she made, every glimmer in her eyes—bright as the morning star—set his heart fluttering and stirred a desire buried deep within him.
But then...
“Phew.”
Hwaran sighed again, and his brow tightened.
He knew what lay behind that sigh. He knew who it was for.
The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.
He repeated the epithet and name silently. Beneath the table, his hand clenched of its own accord.
What’s so special about that bastard?
He had already heard about Hwaran’s connection to Jin Taekyung.

The details of what had happened between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect two months ago had never become widely known. But word had swept through Murim that the Taeeul Merciless Sword, one of Zhongnan’s three greatest masters, had knelt before a young prodigy barely past twenty.
Impossible.
It was something that could not and should not have happened. Hwangbo Ak had dismissed it as a ridiculous rumor and clicked his tongue.
More troubling, though, was his suspicion that the incident had left Hwaran with feelings for Jin Taekyung.
—Are you certain?
Baek Woo perked up at the sudden Sound Transmission.
—Hm?
—I asked whether what you said earlier was certain. The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung. Is the person Young Lady Ju is waiting for really that bastard?
—Do you think she’s waiting for the Successor Beggar?
Even Hwangbo Ak had to admit she wasn’t.
Whatever peculiar tastes Hwaran might have, she couldn’t possibly like Gung Gibang. The man gave off the sour reek of stale dog food just by sitting nearby.
—So it really is that bastard? Are you saying this Young Master is less than a worm that crawled out of some backwater corner of Shanxi Province?

—Not a worm. A Divine Dragon. And Shanxi Province is no longer a backwater corner. It is the hidden residence from which the dragon named Jin Taekyung rose, as well as the center of the trade routes running through northern Gaoyuan.
Having lightly corrected him, Baek Woo continued.
—Fellow Daoist Hwangbo, this isn’t the Jin Family of Taiyuan you used to know. Now that I think about it, I could tell the moment I met the Heaven Shaking Sword.
—The Heaven Shaking Sword? Heaven Shaking Sword Jin Mukyung?
—Is there another Heaven Shaking Sword we both know?
Hwangbo Ak’s eyebrows twitched.
If Ju Hwaran, who kept sighing across the table, and that young escort who looked like he had crawled in from who knew where had not been watching him, he would have scowled long ago.
—Don’t bring up that name. Do you think I’m asking because I don’t know who that bastard is?
—Ah, that’s right. You and the Heaven Shaking Sword were at Heaven’s Gate Temple together—
—Enough. Stop!
—You startled me. All right. Why are you shouting?
Hwangbo Ak’s clenched fist had turned red.
Jin Mukyung. That was a name he would remember until the day he died.
Hwangbo Ak had thought he possessed everything. Jin Mukyung had shown him a wall he could never climb—and humiliated him in the process.
Damn it.
Now the younger brother was standing in his way, too.
Seeing the anger on Hwangbo Ak’s face, Baek Woo moved his lips cautiously.
—Fellow Daoist Hwangbo. May I offer you some advice?
—What now?
—You remember what you said to me. If the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon comes, don’t ever mention it out loud. No—don’t even move your lips.
—Hmph. Worried we might come to blows?
—No, that’s not it. I’m worried I might get dragged into it too.
—...What?
Baek Woo regarded him with a look full of concern and pity.
—If you want to die, die alone.

—You were in closed-door training at your family’s estate during the Star-Array Grand Banquet, so you probably don’t know. But even now, whenever I think about that man, I feel—ugh. Anyway, keep that in mind. Understood?
What in the world was he talking about? Die alone?
Hwangbo Ak remained silent for a moment, staring at Baek Woo in disbelief. Then he sent another Sound Transmission.
—Are you... serious?
—Infinite Life Buddha. I swear before the Primordial Heavenly Venerable that I’m completely serious.
—Have you no pride as a martial artist?
—I lost that at the Star-Array Grand Banquet. Do you know what it’s like to have the top of your head stepped on after using the Cloud-Dragon Eight Forms?
—Even so!
—Even so, no. That man is a monster.
—W-What happened to the Kunlun Cloud Dragon, that proud, lofty crane? Where’s the Baek Woo I knew?
Baek Woo gazed into the past with a nostalgic look in his eyes.

—Come to think of it, the Successor Beggar said something similar to me back then. Then, in the very next test, he was beaten like a dog by Jin Taekyung. You heard what happened, didn’t you? Gung Gibang fell behind in movement technique, his eyes rolled back, and he tried to grab Jin Taekyung by the hair. He nearly got his head knocked off.
—Infinite Life Buddha. Let’s be honest. Do you think everything the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon has done is just a rumor?
—Of course!
Baek Woo let out a quiet sigh at the firm reply.
—Why?
—How could any man do those things? His master, the Fire King, must have handled everything and given his Disciple the credit!
—True. By any ordinary measure, it’s absurd. Reaching Supreme Peak when he’s barely past twenty? How could that be possible?
At last, a sensible answer. Hwangbo Ak nodded with conviction.
—Exactly. The Fire King Jeok Cheongang must have stepped in and handed his Disciple the credit.

—I’m saying this again because I’m worried about you: don’t tell the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon that his master handed him the credit. I don’t want to be paired with you as a battle partner and have my face beaten in.
—...What are you playing at?
—Infinite Life Buddha. It’s simple. Don’t try to reason it out with common sense. Don’t even try to understand it. Just accept it.
For a moment, Baek Woo’s almost enlightened tone left Hwangbo Ak speechless. Then he tried another angle.
—W-Wait. You have feelings for Young Lady Ju too, don’t you?
—Young Lady Ju? Of course I like her. What man wouldn’t?
—That very Young Lady Ju has feelings for Jin Taekyung. And you still intend to protect your rival?
—My life matters more to me than Young Lady Ju. So does my hair.
—What?
Baek Woo checked that no one was looking, then casually dipped his head.
A strangely bare patch showed between the neatly arranged strands at his crown.
—Infinite Life Buddha. See?
—What on earth happened to your—
Hwangbo Ak could not finish his Sound Transmission. Baek Woo gave him a sorrowful smile.
—My hair stopped growing after my head was stepped on during the Star-Array Grand Banquet...
—Give up. Giving up makes life easier. But if you absolutely can’t give up, please do it when I’m not around. I’d like to live, too.
What kind of insane nonsense was this?
Hwangbo Ak swallowed hard.
He was still furious, but a chill ran down his spine. Baek Woo was an old friend and a proud martial artist. If even he was talking like this...
Is this for real?
Hwangbo Ak had never believed all the rumors about the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
But if—if there wasn’t a shred of falsehood in them...
A monster beyond common sense.
Yes. An undeniable monster.
And at the same time, an unbearable humiliation wrapped itself around Hwangbo Ak’s entire body.
What a damnable mess.
His fist tightened. A groan escaped through his parted teeth, and Hwaran, sensing that something was wrong, spoke.
“Young Hero Hwangbo. Is something wrong?”
“Ah, no. Nothing.”
At his strained reply, the young escort who had done nothing but occupy a seat at their table gave a quiet laugh.
“You look very much like something’s wrong.”
“...I said it’s nothing.”
“If you say so. The food here is good, by the way.”
Hwangbo Ak narrowed his eyes.
He had allowed the man to join them only because he was Hwaran’s escort. From his behavior to the way he spoke, everything about him grated on Hwangbo Ak.
A mutter slipped through his twisted lips.
“This is the trouble with people who have no pedigree...”
Ju Hwaran was not a fool. A cold chill passed over her beautiful face, which had been filled with troubled thoughts only a moment earlier.
“Young Hero Hwangbo.”
“Ah, I wouldn’t want Young Lady Ju to misunderstand. I wasn’t talking about that fellow.”
Hwangbo Ak put on a false smile and pointed to a table some distance away.
“I was talking about those bastards who practice demonic, heterodox arts over there.”
And at the moment his voice, neither loud nor soft, rang through the inn—
Scrape.
Someone rose from their seat.
