chapters.title: Chapter 540
paragraphs: They say words have no feet, yet travel a thousand li.
And these days, Henan Province was boiling like a cauldron over a charcoal fire.

Under countless watchful eyes, news that two exceptionally young Divine Dragons had been appointed pavilion masters by special order of the Alliance Leader swept across Henan before two days had passed.
“Have you heard the news?”
“I’ve already heard it, so don’t tell me. Even that yellow dog in the back alley probably knows.”
Whenever two or more people gathered, they talked about the appointments.
Opinions were divided, but many martial artists viewed Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung’s appointments favorably.
“Pavilion masters, huh? Of course. Those two are more than qualified.”
“Still, considering their ages, haven’t they been given too much responsibility?”
“That’s what makes it so impressive. Who else could achieve that kind of might and merit at barely twenty?”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right.”
“Damn it. I can’t stand listening to this.”
“...And who might you be, Brother?”
“Come on. Some people are born into good families, find good masters, learn peerless martial arts, and now they get to be pavilion masters of the Murim Alliance too?”
“By your logic, every young prodigy from the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families would be a Supreme Peak master. And why are you taking it out on us?”
“I got pissed off listening to you, so I butted in.”
But where there was light, there was shadow.

Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung inspired envy as well as admiration. That was true not only of wandering martial artists who had lived rough lives, but also of disciples from prestigious sects and families.
“Damn it. How does this make any sense?”
“There’s nothing we can do. The Alliance Leader himself issued the order. Our Sect Leader told us in no uncertain terms not to say a word about it.”
“And what about you?”

“What good would saying anything do? I’m only a third-generation Disciple. One of my fellow disciples ran his mouth a few shichen ago and paid for it. Our Senior Martial Uncle was furious. He ordered everyone between him and me to assemble, and...”
“I can imagine.”

“Some lunatic even summoned our Master. That really set the mood. We got chewed out until our souls hurt. We even had to hear what we were doing with ourselves when the much younger Blazing Flame Divine Dragon and Huashan Divine Dragon were doing so well.”
“What kind of nonsense is that? Why blame us because those two are monsters?”
“Exactly. It’s not as if they managed it themselves.”
“Wait. Don’t tell me...”
“Are you crazy? I didn’t say it. But before anyone could stop him, the lunatic who’d summoned our Master came out with it: ‘Their masters are the Fire King and the Sword Saint.’”
“Good heavens. Did I hear that right? Look at my arm. I’ve got goose bumps.”
“You think you’re bad? Imagine how I and the other Senior Brothers felt after hearing it directly. Even now, I’ve got goose bumps all the way down to my balls.”
“Just so we’re clear, you don’t need to show me.”
“...I wouldn’t show you even if you begged. Anyway, things are tense because of those two. Though probably not as tense as they are in the Hwangbo Family.”
By then, everyone had heard the rumor that the Shandong Fist Dragon—the Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—had suffered a spectacular disgrace.

He had since been appointed Commander of the Murim Alliance’s Outer Hall. Between that post and Jin Taekyung’s position as a pavilion master directly under the Alliance Leader’s Office lay a gulf as wide as heaven and earth.
“I heard the Hwangbo Family Head met privately with the Alliance Leader and demanded punishment...”
“He went around telling everyone himself, so it’s probably true. As for the result, you already know.”

Hwangbo Gun, the Family Head of the Hwangbo Family, had proudly bragged about his private meeting with the Alliance Leader. Before even half a day had passed, the disciplinary decision arrived, and he had to swallow his humiliation.

I. Jin Taekyung, Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion, privately took one side despite witnessing the dispute before him. He is therefore ordered to fast for a limited period. II. Taishan of the Black Dragon Demon Gate committed two offenses. His first offense was causing a dispute on a main road and harming commoners. His second was disregarding the Alliance’s rules and wielding a weapon first, thereby failing to follow proper procedure. However, eyewitness accounts and testimony establish some justification for his actions. He is ordered to pay each person who suffered losses as a result of his actions ten times the amount of their damages. III. The offense committed by the Shandong Fist Dragon, Hwangbo Ak, is similar to Taishan’s. However, because he was substantially responsible for causing the dispute and made remarks liable to cause trouble, he is ordered to remain under disciplinary confinement for a fixed period.
For Hwangbo Gun, it was enough to drive him mad.
The next day, a rumor spread that Jin Taekyung had polished off ten bowls of gukbap in one sitting and patted his stomach. That only made matters worse.

The orthodox purists who supported Hwangbo Gun voiced their discontent too. But the shadow cast by the giant known as the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was deep, and they could hardly defy the Alliance Leader’s authority over something like this. They had no choice but to swallow their anger.
Amid all that admiration and envy, Jin Taekyung made another extraordinary move just a day after his appointment as Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion.
It began with a single notice pasted conspicuously on a wall beside a busy main road.
“Have you seen it?”
“If you mean the news about the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’ve heard enough to make my ears bleed. Wait. Seen what?”
“About half a shichen ago, some fellow named Hyuk—Hyuk something—put up huge notices all along the main roads.”
“Why would I care what Hyuk-whatsisname did?”
“Because that Hyuk-whatsisname is Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung’s right-hand man. I read the notice, and apparently the Two Dragons Pavilion is recruiting people.”
“What? Is that true?”
“Without a doubt. But the notice is... strange. There are other people here, too, and... No, the whole thing is strange.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“It’s, well... Never mind. Go see and hear it for yourself.”
“...Hear it?”
These days, any news about the Two Dragons Pavilion was a hot topic in Henan.
And now the youngest pavilion master—whose genius and accomplishments were rare even in Murim’s long history—had done something else?
“Ah, I can’t miss this!”
Martial artists with affiliations, martial artists still looking for a place to belong, and even curious commoners came rushing over.
And when they gathered in one place, they finally saw it.
★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★
The words were written in enormous letters beside a bizarre emblem.
The people gathered before it like clouds all widened their eyes and cried out in astonishment.
“Th-That!”
“Good heavens!”
How could a phrase be so simple, so easy to grasp, and so bold? The lines beneath it caught the eye just as readily.
Recruitment Requirements
First: Someone with the passion to do whatever they set their mind to.
Second: An upright character.
Third: At least the level of injuring others with Sword Energy.
\# Recruiting around the clock \# No one below Peak need apply \# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter \# Age doesn’t matter \# Life begins at eighty \# Hey, you can do it too.
Every line was outrageous!
Simply reading those magnificent words was enough to set blood surging and hearts pounding. Shouts erupted from the crowd.
“Yeah! I can do it too!”
“You too? Me too!”
“Aaaah! The Two Dragons Pavilion is calling me!”
“Damn it! The level of injuring others with Sword Energy!”
Hundreds of people who had read the notice were cheering or groaning when—
Ting-a-ling.
A clear, lively melody rang out from somewhere.
The crowd parted as though by prior agreement. A group appeared and passed through them, walking as if on clouds.
“What’s that...?”
“Isn’t that the band from Honghakru?”
“Why would a band show up here?”
It was one of the ten most famous bands in Henan, and its sudden arrival left everyone bewildered.
Then a breathtakingly beautiful woman appeared before the crowd and smiled.
“Hongmae? It’s Hongmae!”
“Waaaaah!”

Hongmae was Honghakru’s most beautiful singer, a singing courtesan famous for her enchanting voice. She bowed her head with graceful poise, then gave a meaningful glance. The musicians took their cue and began to play.
Ting-a-ling. Chaarang!
The melody was bright and lively.
And the moment the first line flowed from her lips, the martial artists there understood as if under a spell.
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my era of success begins~”
If they wanted to succeed, they had to join the Two Dragons Pavilion.
I’d always been this way. No particular reason—I’d just never liked songs or children all that much.
But today was an exception.
“Heh heh. Those little rascals.”
I smiled contentedly as I listened to the sounds coming through the gap in the window.
Outside, children who looked to be around elementary school age were running around energetically and singing.
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my era of success begins~!”
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and now more sects are looking for me~!”
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my life has changed~!”
“A new era, a new hero!”
“The Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion!”
The ending was perfect, too.
I gave myself a little round of applause, then noticed Hyuk Mujin staring at me in disbelief.
“What is it, you bastard?”
“...I’m just stunned. I’ve never seen or heard of anything like this.”
“What do you think? Innovative, isn’t it?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded reluctantly.
“It definitely works. I just went around checking, and it’s chaos out there. You’d think Dark Heaven had invaded.”
“I knew it would work. Heh heh.”
“That song in particular... It’s everywhere. People are saying you’ve released poison into Murim, Captain.”
“What’s that supposed to mean? What poison?”
“They say it’s more addictive than opium.”
“Oh. Ohoho.”
Ah, how satisfying.

What a rewarding outcome. A certain cyber university in Seoul might sue me for plagiarism, but this was Murim. ([Audio reference](https://www.youtube.com/results? search_query=%EC%84%9C%EC%9A%B8%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EB%B2%84%EB%8C%80%ED%95%99%EA%B5%90+%EB%82%98%EC%9D%98+%EC%84%B1%EA%B3%B5+%EC%8B%9C%EB%8C%80+%EC%8B%9C%EC%9E%91%EB%90%90%EB%8B%A4))
I’m sorry, and thank you. I’ll put the song to good use.
And so the greatest hit of the era was born, destined to mercilessly assault the eardrums of these primitive Murim bumpkins.
I still got a thrill remembering the bandleader’s and singer’s faces when I’d given them the melody I’d hastily come up with.
They looked like primitive humans discovering fire.
Was this how Prometheus had felt in Greek mythology?
The difference was that, instead of donating my organs to an eagle sent by Zeus, I had to deal with the flood of applicants.
“How is the application process? Are you done?”
Hyuk Mujin looked at me as though I’d lost my mind.
“Are you serious?”
“More than I expected, huh?”
“It’s insane. Completely insane. There are so many, I’m starting to wonder if Dark Heaven sent in applications too.”
Hmm. It seemed to be even more effective than I’d imagined.
I’d added the requirement of being a Peak master in case something like this happened, but the world was vast, and apparently it had plenty of masters.
“Then let’s do this. First...”
I’d just finished thinking it over and begun to speak when—
Crash!
The door broke apart, and someone appeared.
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion. My era of success begins.”
The most ominous song in the world. A chilling expression.
I froze when I met those glowing red eyes. Fire King Jeok Cheongang spat out his next words.
“This old man nearly suffered qi deviation because of that damn song.”
“...Welcome.”

sentences.text: They say words have no feet, yet travel a thousand li.
And these days, Henan Province was boiling like a cauldron over a charcoal fire.

Under countless watchful eyes, news that two exceptionally young Divine Dragons had been appointed pavilion masters by special order of the Alliance Leader swept across Henan before two days had passed.
“Have you heard the news?”
“I’ve already heard it, so don’t tell me.
Even that yellow dog in the back alley probably knows.”
Whenever two or more people gathered, they talked about the appointments.
Opinions were divided, but many martial artists viewed Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung’s appointments favorably.
“Pavilion masters, huh?
Of course.
Those two are more than qualified.”
“Still, considering their ages, haven’t they been given too much responsibility?”
“That’s what makes it so impressive.
Who else could achieve that kind of might and merit at barely twenty?”
“Now that you mention it, you’re right.”
“Damn it.
I can’t stand listening to this.”
“...And who might you be, Brother?”
“Come on.
Some people are born into good families, find good masters, learn peerless martial arts, and now they get to be pavilion masters of the Murim Alliance too?”
“By your logic, every young prodigy from the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families would be a Supreme Peak master.
And why are you taking it out on us?”
“I got pissed off listening to you, so I butted in.”
But where there was light, there was shadow.
Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung inspired envy as well as admiration.
That was true not only of wandering martial artists who had lived rough lives, but also of disciples from prestigious sects and families.
“Damn it.
How does this make any sense?”
“There’s nothing we can do.
The Alliance Leader himself issued the order.
Our Sect Leader told us in no uncertain terms not to say a word about it.”
“And what about you?”
“What good would saying anything do?
I’m only a third-generation Disciple.
One of my fellow disciples ran his mouth a few shichen ago and paid for it.
Our Senior Martial Uncle was furious.
He ordered everyone between him and me to assemble, and...”
“I can imagine.”
“Some lunatic even summoned our Master.
That really set the mood.
We got chewed out until our souls hurt.
We even had to hear what we were doing with ourselves when the much younger Blazing Flame Divine Dragon and Huashan Divine Dragon were doing so well.”
“What kind of nonsense is that?
Why blame us because those two are monsters?”
“Exactly.
It’s not as if they managed it themselves.”
“Wait.
Don’t tell me...”
“Are you crazy?
I didn’t say it.
But before anyone could stop him, the lunatic who’d summoned our Master came out with it: ‘Their masters are the Fire King and the Sword Saint.’”
“Good heavens.
Did I hear that right?
Look at my arm.
I’ve got goose bumps.”
“You think you’re bad?
Imagine how I and the other Senior Brothers felt after hearing it directly.
Even now, I’ve got goose bumps all the way down to my balls.”
“Just so we’re clear, you don’t need to show me.”
“...I wouldn’t show you even if you begged.
Anyway, things are tense because of those two.
Though probably not as tense as they are in the Hwangbo Family.”
By then, everyone had heard the rumor that the Shandong Fist Dragon—the Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—had suffered a spectacular disgrace.
He had since been appointed Commander of the Murim Alliance’s Outer Hall.
Between that post and Jin Taekyung’s position as a pavilion master directly under the Alliance Leader’s Office lay a gulf as wide as heaven and earth.
“I heard the Hwangbo Family Head met privately with the Alliance Leader and demanded punishment...”
“He went around telling everyone himself, so it’s probably true.
As for the result, you already know.”
Hwangbo Gun, the Family Head of the Hwangbo Family, had proudly bragged about his private meeting with the Alliance Leader.
Before even half a day had passed, the disciplinary decision arrived, and he had to swallow his humiliation.
I.
Jin Taekyung, Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion, privately took one side despite witnessing the dispute before him.
He is therefore ordered to fast for a limited period.
II.
Taishan of the Black Dragon Demon Gate committed two offenses.
His first offense was causing a dispute on a main road and harming commoners.
His second was disregarding the Alliance’s rules and wielding a weapon first, thereby failing to follow proper procedure.
However, eyewitness accounts and testimony establish some justification for his actions.
He is ordered to pay each person who suffered losses as a result of his actions ten times the amount of their damages.
III.
The offense committed by the Shandong Fist Dragon, Hwangbo Ak, is similar to Taishan’s.
However, because he was substantially responsible for causing the dispute and made remarks liable to cause trouble, he is ordered to remain under disciplinary confinement for a fixed period.
For Hwangbo Gun, it was enough to drive him mad.
The next day, a rumor spread that Jin Taekyung had polished off ten bowls of gukbap in one sitting and patted his stomach.
That only made matters worse.
The orthodox purists who supported Hwangbo Gun voiced their discontent too.
But the shadow cast by the giant known as the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was deep, and they could hardly defy the Alliance Leader’s authority over something like this.
They had no choice but to swallow their anger.
Amid all that admiration and envy, Jin Taekyung made another extraordinary move just a day after his appointment as Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion.
It began with a single notice pasted conspicuously on a wall beside a busy main road.
“Have you seen it?”
“If you mean the news about the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’ve heard enough to make my ears bleed.
Wait.
Seen what?”
“About half a shichen ago, some fellow named Hyuk—Hyuk something—put up huge notices all along the main roads.”
“Why would I care what Hyuk-whatsisname did?”
“Because that Hyuk-whatsisname is Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung’s right-hand man.
I read the notice, and apparently the Two Dragons Pavilion is recruiting people.”
“What?
Is that true?”
“Without a doubt.
But the notice is... strange.
There are other people here, too, and...
No, the whole thing is strange.”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“It’s, well...
Never mind.
Go see and hear it for yourself.”
“...Hear it?”
These days, any news about the Two Dragons Pavilion was a hot topic in Henan.
And now the youngest pavilion master—whose genius and accomplishments were rare even in Murim’s long history—had done something else?
“Ah, I can’t miss this!”
Martial artists with affiliations, martial artists still looking for a place to belong, and even curious commoners came rushing over.
And when they gathered in one place, they finally saw it.
★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★
The words were written in enormous letters beside a bizarre emblem.
The people gathered before it like clouds all widened their eyes and cried out in astonishment.
“Th-That!”
“Good heavens!”
How could a phrase be so simple, so easy to grasp, and so bold?
The lines beneath it caught the eye just as readily.
Recruitment Requirements
First: Someone with the passion to do whatever they set their mind to.
Second: An upright character.
Third: At least the level of injuring others with Sword Energy.
\# Recruiting around the clock \# No one below Peak need apply \# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter \# Age doesn’t matter \# Life begins at eighty \# Hey, you can do it too.
Every line was outrageous!
Simply reading those magnificent words was enough to set blood surging and hearts pounding.
Shouts erupted from the crowd.
“Yeah!
I can do it too!”
“You too?
Me too!”
“Aaaah!
The Two Dragons Pavilion is calling me!”
“Damn it!
The level of injuring others with Sword Energy!”
Hundreds of people who had read the notice were cheering or groaning when—
Ting-a-ling.
A clear, lively melody rang out from somewhere.
The crowd parted as though by prior agreement.
A group appeared and passed through them, walking as if on clouds.
“What’s that...?”
“Isn’t that the band from Honghakru?”
“Why would a band show up here?”
It was one of the ten most famous bands in Henan, and its sudden arrival left everyone bewildered.
Then a breathtakingly beautiful woman appeared before the crowd and smiled.
“Hongmae?
It’s Hongmae!”
“Waaaaah!”
Hongmae was Honghakru’s most beautiful singer, a singing courtesan famous for her enchanting voice.
She bowed her head with graceful poise, then gave a meaningful glance.
The musicians took their cue and began to play.
Ting-a-ling.
Chaarang!
The melody was bright and lively.
And the moment the first line flowed from her lips, the martial artists there understood as if under a spell.
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my era of success begins~”
If they wanted to succeed, they had to join the Two Dragons Pavilion.
I’d always been this way.
No particular reason—I’d just never liked songs or children all that much.
But today was an exception.
“Heh heh.
Those little rascals.”
I smiled contentedly as I listened to the sounds coming through the gap in the window.
Outside, children who looked to be around elementary school age were running around energetically and singing.
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my era of success begins~!”
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and now more sects are looking for me~!”
“Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and my life has changed~!”
“A new era, a new hero!”
“The Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion!”
The ending was perfect, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 541
paragraphs: Henan was a land with a long and storied history.

It was home to sprawling thousand-year-old capitals such as Kaifeng and Luoyang, cities that had served as the seats of numerous dynasties. It also offered breathtaking natural scenery and all sorts of famous landmarks, including four great mountains.
Visitors came year-round. Naturally, there were plenty of inns, pleasure houses, and other places for entertainment and lodging.
But the old innkeeper, whose family had run the same inn for three generations, could confidently say this street had never been so crowded.
What in the world...?
He stared around in bewilderment at a veritable sea of people.
“Hey, wait a minute! Don’t try to cut in line!”
“Who keeps shoving me?”
“You little pup. You’ve been giving me insolent looks for a while now. Do I have to show you a coffin before you come to your senses?”
“What did you say? I was willing to let it go, but this lowly wandering martial artist is—”
“Heh heh. Everyone’s certainly full of energy. It’s a pleasant sight.”
“Pleasant? It’s been so noisy that I can hardly stand it.”
A wandering martial artist who looked like a wild wolf and a man who appeared to be the scion of a prestigious family glared at each other.
The sight made a half-gray-haired middle-aged man burst into hearty laughter, while a beautiful woman whose age was impossible to guess clicked her tongue.
Countless others stood farther away, watching and whispering among themselves.
What on earth is going on here?
In the middle of the chaos, just as the innkeeper felt his soul halfway leaving his body, a voice reached his ears.
“There’s no need to worry so much.”
“Pardon?”
“Not over there. This way.”
The innkeeper turned again in surprise. An old man sat at a table, leisurely sipping from a wine cup while everyone else waited in line.
“They have their own reasons for being here. There won’t be any serious trouble.”
He was small, with an unruly white beard and a face flushed red with drink.
For a moment, the innkeeper wondered if he might be a martial artist. But he looked for all the world like an ordinary old drunk. The innkeeper gave him a discreet glance, then lowered his voice.
“W-What in the world is going on?”
“They’re all people who want to begin their era of success. You must have heard that song, too. ‘Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and—’”
The old man began humming a lively tune.
The innkeeper’s shoulders instinctively began to sway. Then his eyes widened.
“Ah. Are you talking about that... Two Dragons Pavilion?”
“You got it. The young Pavilion Master of that Two Dragons Pavilion is staying right here.”
“Good heavens.”
The innkeeper let out a short gasp.

He had known that the person staying in the detached building was a young knight-errant famous throughout the martial world. But he had never imagined that he was the Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion everyone was talking about.
“So that’s why so many martial artists have come here. But even so, I never imagined there would be this many...”
“Heh heh. Isn’t it a fine opportunity? It’s rare to find a place that doesn’t care about your background, gender, or age.”
“That’s true. I heard even an eighty-year-old can apply.”
The old man answered quietly.
“As it happens, that’s exactly what I intend to do.”
“Hahaha! You certainly know how to make a joke.”
“Does that sound like a joke?”
“Pardon?”
“I asked whether that sounded like a joke.”
The innkeeper’s laughter stopped. He stared at the old man, his eyes trembling.
“Th-Then, old man—I mean, sir—you’re applying too?”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
The old man wiped his wine-soaked beard with his sleeve. As his robe shifted, a worn scabbard showed beneath it.
“I’m a martial artist too. Like them. Unlike you.”
“Gasp.”
“There’s no need to be so frightened. This old man doesn’t lay a hand on commoners.”
He paused to consider something, then added softly, “Most of the time.”
Not a trace of drunkenness remained in his gentle voice, and for an instant, his eyes held the ferocity of a wild beast.
The innkeeper felt a chill and took an involuntary step back. Just then, someone began coming down the stairs.
Step. Step.
The old man’s eyes flashed.
“Is it about to begin?”
He was not the only one who thought so. The dozens of Peak masters waiting in line and the spectators who seemed to outnumber them ten to one all fell silent.
Someone appeared on the stairs.
“How many people have come—whoa! You startled me.”
The young man, Hyuk Mujin, jumped in surprise. A flicker of disappointment crossed the faces of those watching.
But the Peak masters, who had sensed his aura long before he appeared, merely muttered calmly.
“He’s not the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
“He sent a messenger down in his place. Is he already throwing his weight around?”
“He’s impressive for a messenger. With that kind of aura at his age, he’s better than most second-generation Disciples from prestigious sects.”
“I agree. And if it’s the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, I suppose he can send someone in his place.”
Hyuk Mujin looked sourly at the enormous crowd murmuring around him and cleared his throat.
“Ahem. The Captain—I mean, the Pavilion Master—has ordered me to begin the interviews. I’ll call you by name, one at a time. Please follow me when your turn comes.”

Reaching the Peak realm meant being recognized as a master anywhere in Murim. The Peak masters all took pride in their abilities, and they were plainly unhappy to be told to wait again. But none complained.
A thirsty man had to dig his own well. Having come here, they had to put up with it.
“I understand perfectly well, so stop spouting nonsense and call the names already.”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened at the rough-looking middle-aged wandering martial artist.
“Oh. It’s true.”
“What is?”
“Ah, it’s nothing. The Pavilion Master told me to reject anyone who uses informal speech and acts rudely the first time they meet someone, no exceptions. I didn’t expect to find someone so quickly.”
“...What?”
“Let’s see. You’re Great Hero No Guisan, the Black Blood Saber, correct? You may go home now.”
The Black Blood Saber blinked at him in silence, then roared.
“What kind of bullshit rule is that?”
Hyuk Mujin pulled a bamboo slip bearing the man’s personal details from the purse at his waist and nodded.
“It’s right here. That kind of rule.”
“I waited an entire shichen!”
“Oh dear. That’s unfortunate.”
“You insolent little bastard! You think you can act this arrogantly because your master’s behind you? Do you really think you’ll be safe after this?”
“I think I’ll probably be fine.”
“You little—!”
“If you keep this up, our Pavilion Master will come down himself and say, ‘You bastard!’”
What kind of person was this?
The Black Blood Saber and everyone watching stood with their mouths open.

The Black Blood Saber was a formidable fighter, renowned even among the rough-and-tumble wandering martial artists. People said that if not for his foul temper, he could become the Sect Leader of a school that very day and build it into a mid-level sect.
Yet Hyuk Mujin did not so much as blink before the aura he released.
“You’re rejected. Off you go.”
For Hyuk Mujin, who had followed Jin Taekyung around and suffered every kind of hell, his composure was only natural. It left even the foul-tempered Black Blood Saber speechless.
That was when—
“Ha! Hahaha!”
Rumble!
A booming laugh erupted from somewhere. The air burst outward, and the ground trembled in tiny shudders.
The Peak masters went rigid as they sensed the source of the overwhelming aura pressing down on them.
What incredible internal energy...!
One level above me. No—two levels.
What in the world...?
Every horrified gaze turned toward the old man who had been leisurely sipping his wine moments earlier. He was slowly rising from his seat.
“Don’t make such a commotion. Don’t you feel sorry for the innkeeper?”
He smiled gently at the innkeeper, who lay facedown and trembling. Someone in the crowd cried out, almost screaming.
“O-Old Man Ilyang!”
Old Man Ilyang. Those three words were enough.

He was a master who stood between the orthodox and unorthodox paths and had once dominated an era. His was the sobriquet of a monster who had burned countless opponents to death with his mighty Scorching Yang Qi.
The sudden appearance of a Supreme Peak master froze the entire gathering.
Is that truly Old Man Ilyang?
Th-That old monster... What is he doing here?
No one present could compare to him. It was doubtful they could bring him down even if they all attacked together.
Only one wall separated Peak from Supreme Peak. The distance across it was vast.
Step. Step.
Old Man Ilyang walked leisurely through the silence, then looked at Hyuk Mujin and smiled.
“Go and tell him this old man wishes to meet him.”
Another ripple of shock passed through the crowd.
Old Man Ilyang, of all people, wanted to join the Two Dragons Pavilion under a Pavilion Master barely more than a boy. That alone was astonishing. Yet he had made his request so courteously.
“U-Understood. Please wait a moment.”
Hyuk Mujin turned away, flustered. He did not see the ominous heat in Old Man Ilyang’s eyes.
The Fire Gate Clan. The Fire Gate Clan, huh? Heh heh. At long last, an opportunity has come even to this old man.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung? Whether the rumors about him were true did not matter.
He was still a brat barely past twenty. At Old Man Ilyang’s age, he had no intention whatsoever of respectfully serving such a fledgling as his superior. But...
The Fire Gate Clan’s divine technique, passed down to only one person each generation. I will make it mine, whatever it takes.
He had spent his life pursuing strength, yet had never reached the pinnacle of Scorching Yang Qi.
With the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts, he could. He could even claim the title of greatest under heaven.
According to reliable rumors, Fire King Jeok Cheongang won’t be joining the Two Dragons Pavilion. That leaves only his young Disciple and the other riffraff.
The moment the Two Dragons Pavilion received a mission and left Henan would be his chance.
Dark Heaven? The Murim Alliance? What did he care what became of Murim’s fate?
The corner of his mouth, covered in age spots, twitched.
“Heh heh. Hahaha.”
Before Old Man Ilyang’s eyes, the five characters for greatest under heaven were already shimmering.
Eighty-five years old.
Name: Won Cheol.
Sobriquet: Old Man Ilyang.
His martial arts realm was Supreme Peak.
It was a practically perfect profile, without a single thing to criticize.
But the special judge he had suddenly found himself facing had a different opinion.
“He’s got the eyes of a bastard who’d stab you in the back the first chance he got.”
“Pardon?”
There was no need to ask what he meant. Jeok Cheongang had already closed the distance and was smashing his fist into Old Man Ilyang’s mouth.
Whoosh!
Extreme Yang energy surged from the blow, enough to turn anything in its path to ash.
Old Man Ilyang sucked in a sharp breath and hurriedly crossed his arms to block it, but the difference in strength was obvious.
That’s bad.
Even Scorching Yang Qi had its levels. If Old Man Ilyang’s qi was an ordinary flame, Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s was lava.
That difference became clear in an instant.
Crunch. Wham!
Bones shattered, and Old Man Ilyang’s eyes lost focus.
I watched with genuine regret and shouted, “No! The ace—!”
But once Jeok Cheongang’s fist began spitting fire, it did not stop.
Wham! Wham! Wham-wham-wham!
Arms, legs, stomach, back, face.
As if to show off his regained youth, he drove qi-packed punches into every part of Old Man Ilyang’s body. With each blow, tangible Scorching Yang Qi enveloped the area.
Wow. I’m seeing the pit of fire right here.
Was this audition genre hip-hop?
One Sun—no, Old Man Ilyang, who had not even received a necklace, lost consciousness without managing a single proper counterattack.
Thud.

Old Man Ilyang collapsed like crumbling ash. Jeok Cheongang stood looking down at him, then muttered, “Now I remember this bastard. He’s the son of a bitch who said he was after our sect’s martial arts.”
“...I’m glad you had a reason, at least. I thought you’d gone mad, Old Master.”
“Better late than never. I can’t stand the sight of him, so get him out of here.”
Not long after Old Man Ilyang’s corpse—or rather, his body—was carried away, a commotion broke out outside.
I glanced through the window. Terrified applicants were fleeing, even using their movement techniques to get away.
“...Oh, for fuck’s sake.”
Do they have any idea what it took to arrange this? The audition was completely fucked. Seriously.
Jeok Cheongang caught my resentful look and answered bluntly.
“What do you want me to do?”
“You could’ve gone a little easier on him. Wanting to get his hands on some martial arts isn’t a capital crime. He hadn’t actually done anything yet. You could’ve just rejected him quietly.”
“Tsk, tsk. What an innocent fool. People like that always cause trouble eventually. You have to stamp out a spark before it becomes a fire.”
“...Don’t people usually say you should uproot weeds?”
“You can leave weeds alone. A spark can burn down a mountain.”
I mean, what was he, the chairman of a forest conservation society?
I was muttering inwardly in disbelief when Jeok Cheongang continued.
“What now?”
He jerked his chin toward the window.
“When someone leaves, someone else comes.”
“Huh?”

Countless others stood farther away, watching and whispering among themselves.
What on earth is going on here?
In the middle of the chaos, just as the innkeeper felt his soul halfway leaving his body, a voice reached his ears.
“There’s no need to worry so much.”
“Pardon?”
“Not over there.
This way.”
The innkeeper turned again in surprise.
An old man sat at a table, leisurely sipping from a wine cup while everyone else waited in line.
“They have their own reasons for being here.
There won’t be any serious trouble.”
He was small, with an unruly white beard and a face flushed red with drink.
For a moment, the innkeeper wondered if he might be a martial artist.
But he looked for all the world like an ordinary old drunk.
The innkeeper gave him a discreet glance, then lowered his voice.
“W-What in the world is going on?”
“They’re all people who want to begin their era of success.
You must have heard that song, too.
‘Join the Murim Alliance’s Two Dragons Pavilion, and—’”
The old man began humming a lively tune.
The innkeeper’s shoulders instinctively began to sway.
Then his eyes widened.
“Ah.
Are you talking about that...
Two Dragons Pavilion?”
“You got it.
The young Pavilion Master of that Two Dragons Pavilion is staying right here.”
“Good heavens.”
The innkeeper let out a short gasp.
He had known that the person staying in the detached building was a young knight-errant famous throughout the martial world.
But he had never imagined that he was the Pavilion Master of the Two Dragons Pavilion everyone was talking about.
“So that’s why so many martial artists have come here.
But even so, I never imagined there would be this many...”
“Heh heh.
Isn’t it a fine opportunity?
It’s rare to find a place that doesn’t care about your background, gender, or age.”
“That’s true.
I heard even an eighty-year-old can apply.”
The old man answered quietly.
“As it happens, that’s exactly what I intend to do.”
“Hahaha!
You certainly know how to make a joke.”
“Does that sound like a joke?”
“Pardon?”
“I asked whether that sounded like a joke.”
The innkeeper’s laughter stopped.
He stared at the old man, his eyes trembling.
“Th-Then, old man—I mean, sir—you’re applying too?”
“Isn’t that obvious?”
The old man wiped his wine-soaked beard with his sleeve.
As his robe shifted, a worn scabbard showed beneath it.
“I’m a martial artist too.
Like them.
Unlike you.”
“Gasp.”
“There’s no need to be so frightened.
This old man doesn’t lay a hand on commoners.”
He paused to consider something, then added softly, “Most of the time.”
Not a trace of drunkenness remained in his gentle voice, and for an instant, his eyes held the ferocity of a wild beast.
The innkeeper felt a chill and took an involuntary step back.
Just then, someone began coming down the stairs.
Step.
Step.
The old man’s eyes flashed.
“Is it about to begin?”
He was not the only one who thought so.
The dozens of Peak masters waiting in line and the spectators who seemed to outnumber them ten to one all fell silent.
Someone appeared on the stairs.
“How many people have come—whoa!
You startled me.”
The young man, Hyuk Mujin, jumped in surprise.
A flicker of disappointment crossed the faces of those watching.
But the Peak masters, who had sensed his aura long before he appeared, merely muttered calmly.
“He’s not the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
“He sent a messenger down in his place.
Is he already throwing his weight around?”
“He’s impressive for a messenger.
With that kind of aura at his age, he’s better than most second-generation Disciples from prestigious sects.”
“I agree.
And if it’s the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, I suppose he can send someone in his place.”
Hyuk Mujin looked sourly at the enormous crowd murmuring around him and cleared his throat.
“Ahem.
The Captain—I mean, the Pavilion Master—has ordered me to begin the interviews.
I’ll call you by name, one at a time.
Please follow me when your turn comes.”
Reaching the Peak realm meant being recognized as a master anywhere in Murim.
The Peak masters all took pride in their abilities, and they were plainly unhappy to be told to wait again.
But none complained.
A thirsty man had to dig his own well.
Having come here, they had to put up with it.
“I understand perfectly well, so stop spouting nonsense and call the names already.”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened at the rough-looking middle-aged wandering martial artist.
“Oh.
It’s true.”
“What is?”
“Ah, it’s nothing.
The Pavilion Master told me to reject anyone who uses informal speech and acts rudely the first time they meet someone, no exceptions.
I didn’t expect to find someone so quickly.”
“...What?”
“Let’s see.
You’re Great Hero No Guisan, the Black Blood Saber, correct?
You may go home now.”
The Black Blood Saber blinked at him in silence, then roared.
“What kind of bullshit rule is that?”
Hyuk Mujin pulled a bamboo slip bearing the man’s personal details from the purse at his waist and nodded.
“It’s right here.
That kind of rule.”
“I waited an entire shichen!”
“Oh dear.
That’s unfortunate.”
“You insolent little bastard!
You think you can act this arrogantly because your master’s behind you?
Do you really think you’ll be safe after this?”
“I think I’ll probably be fine.”
“You little—!”
“If you keep this up, our Pavilion Master will come down himself and say, ‘You bastard!’”
What kind of person was this?
The Black Blood Saber and everyone watching stood with their mouths open.
The Black Blood Saber was a formidable fighter, renowned even among the rough-and-tumble wandering martial artists.
People said that if not for his foul temper, he could become the Sect Leader of a school that very day and build it into a mid-level sect.
Yet Hyuk Mujin did not so much as blink before the aura he released.
“You’re rejected.
Off you go.”
For Hyuk Mujin, who had followed Jin Taekyung around and suffered every kind of hell, his composure was only natural.
It left even the foul-tempered Black Blood Saber speechless.
That was when—
“Ha!
Hahaha!”
Rumble!
A booming laugh erupted from somewhere.
The air burst outward, and the ground trembled in tiny shudders.
The Peak masters went rigid as they sensed the source of the overwhelming aura pressing down on them.
What incredible internal energy...!
One level above me.
No—two levels.
What in the world...?
Every horrified gaze turned toward the old man who had been leisurely sipping his wine moments earlier.
He was slowly rising from his seat.
“Don’t make such a commotion.
Don’t you feel sorry for the innkeeper?”
He smiled gently at the innkeeper, who lay facedown and trembling.
Someone in the crowd cried out, almost screaming.
“O-Old Man Ilyang!”
Old Man Ilyang.
Those three words were enough.
He was a master who stood between the orthodox and unorthodox paths and had once dominated an era.
His was the sobriquet of a monster who had burned countless opponents to death with his mighty Scorching Yang Qi.
The sudden appearance of a Supreme Peak master froze the entire gathering.
Is that truly Old Man Ilyang?
Th-That old monster...
What is he doing here?
No one present could compare to him.
It was doubtful they could bring him down even if they all attacked together.
Only one wall separated Peak from Supreme Peak.
The distance across it was vast.
Step.
Step.
Old Man Ilyang walked leisurely through the silence, then looked at Hyuk Mujin and smiled.
“Go and tell him this old man wishes to meet him.”
Another ripple of shock passed through the crowd.
Old Man Ilyang, of all people, wanted to join the Two Dragons Pavilion under a Pavilion Master barely more than a boy.
That alone was astonishing.
Yet he had made his request so courteously.
“U-Understood.
Please wait a moment.”
Hyuk Mujin turned away, flustered.
He did not see the ominous heat in Old Man Ilyang’s eyes.
The Fire Gate Clan.
The Fire Gate Clan, huh?
Heh heh.
At long last, an opportunity has come even to this old man.
Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung?
Whether the rumors about him were true did not matter.
He was still a brat barely past twenty.
At Old Man Ilyang’s age, he had no intention whatsoever of respectfully serving such a fledgling as his superior.
But...
The Fire Gate Clan’s divine technique, passed down to only one person each generation.
I will make it mine, whatever it takes.
He had spent his life pursuing strength, yet had never reached the pinnacle of Scorching Yang Qi.
With the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts, he could.
He could even claim the title of greatest under heaven.
According to reliable rumors, Fire King Jeok Cheongang won’t be joining the Two Dragons Pavilion.
That leaves only his young Disciple and the other riffraff.
The moment the Two Dragons Pavilion received a mission and left Henan would be his chance.
Dark Heaven?
The Murim Alliance?
What did he care what became of Murim’s fate?
The corner of his mouth, covered in age spots, twitched.
“Heh heh.
Hahaha.”
Before Old Man Ilyang’s eyes, the five characters for greatest under heaven were already shimmering.
Eighty-five years old.
Name: Won Cheol.
Sobriquet: Old Man Ilyang.
His martial arts realm was Supreme Peak.
It was a practically perfect profile, without a single thing to criticize.
But the special judge he had suddenly found himself facing had a different opinion.
“He’s got the eyes of a bastard who’d stab you in the back the first chance he got.”
“Pardon?”
There was no need to ask what he meant.
Jeok Cheongang had already closed the distance and was smashing his fist into Old Man Ilyang’s mouth.
Whoosh!
Extreme Yang energy surged from the blow, enough to turn anything in its path to ash.
Old Man Ilyang sucked in a sharp breath and hurriedly crossed his arms to block it, but the difference in strength was obvious.
That’s bad.
Even Scorching Yang Qi had its levels.
If Old Man Ilyang’s qi was an ordinary flame, Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s was lava.
That difference became clear in an instant.
Crunch.
Wham!
Bones shattered, and Old Man Ilyang’s eyes lost focus.
I watched with genuine regret and shouted, “No!
The ace—!”
But once Jeok Cheongang’s fist began spitting fire, it did not stop.
Wham!
Wham!
Wham-wham-wham!
Arms, legs, stomach, back, face.
As if to show off his regained youth, he drove qi-packed punches into every part of Old Man Ilyang’s body.
With each blow, tangible Scorching Yang Qi enveloped the area.
Wow.
I’m seeing the pit of fire right here.
Was this audition genre hip-hop?
One Sun—no, Old Man Ilyang, who had not even received a necklace, lost consciousness without managing a single proper counterattack.
Thud.
Old Man Ilyang collapsed like crumbling ash.
Jeok Cheongang stood looking down at him, then muttered, “Now I remember this bastard.
He’s the son of a bitch who said he was after our sect’s martial arts.”
“...I’m glad you had a reason, at least.
I thought you’d gone mad, Old Master.”
“Better late than never.
I can’t stand the sight of him, so get him out of here.”
Not long after Old Man Ilyang’s corpse—or rather, his body—was carried away, a commotion broke out outside.
I glanced through the window.
Terrified applicants were fleeing, even using their movement techniques to get away.
“...Oh, for fuck’s sake.”
Do they have any idea what it took to arrange this?
The audition was completely fucked.
Seriously.
Jeok Cheongang caught my resentful look and answered bluntly.
“What do you want me to do?”
“You could’ve gone a little easier on him.
Wanting to get his hands on some martial arts isn’t a capital crime.
He hadn’t actually done anything yet.
You could’ve just rejected him quietly.”
“Tsk, tsk.
What an innocent fool.
People like that always cause trouble eventually.
You have to stamp out a spark before it becomes a fire.”
“...Don’t people usually say you should uproot weeds?”
“You can leave weeds alone.
A spark can burn down a mountain.”
I mean, what was he, the chairman of a forest conservation society?
I was muttering inwardly in disbelief when Jeok Cheongang continued.
“What now?”
He jerked his chin toward the window.
“When someone leaves, someone else comes.”
“Huh?”

chapters.title: Chapter 542
paragraphs: You could tell a lot about a person from the way they walked.
That was especially true of martial artists. Their footsteps revealed more than most people would think.

Someone who relied on brute strength in their martial arts tended to walk heavily and roughly. Someone who practiced a more graceful art—or worked as an assassin—might move so lightly you could barely hear them.
Whoever was coming up the stairs now wasn’t just announcing his presence. His footsteps were practically screaming it.
Thud. Thud. Thud.
Listen to that.
The noise was heavy enough to make an ordinary person’s heart sink. With every step, the solidly built staircase creaked and a faint tremor ran through the floor.
Jeok Cheongang had already taken the gourd from his side and begun sipping from it. He spoke with a grave expression.
“Dark Heaven. Now they’re turning people into monsters. What sort of trick did they use?”
“Huh?”
For a moment, I had no idea what he meant. Then I understood and waved a hand.
“Sorry to interrupt, but the guy coming up isn’t from Dark Heaven.”
“Hmm. He’s no one to worry about, regardless. Knock him down as soon as he opens the door and comes in. Hand him over to the Murim Alliance, and we may get something useful out of him.”
“...He’s not from Dark Heaven. And you already smashed the door, Old Master. What door are you talking about?”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes went wide as he spoke, spraying spit.
“You mean that fellow coming up is a pure human?”
“Amazingly, he’s all-natural.”
“Well, you do see some things if you live long enough. The qi I sense from him isn’t particularly pure, though.”
Hyuk Mujin had returned after taking the injured man downstairs. Wiping his palm, still slick with Old Man Ilyang’s blood, on his trouser leg, he answered.
“Ah, as expected of Great Hero Jeok. You recognized demonic, heterodox arts at once.”
“Demonic, heterodox arts?”
“Yes. The Young Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate and his subordinate.”
The thundering footsteps had drowned out the other sound, but there had been two people coming up from the start.
At last, they appeared through the doorway Jeok Cheongang had blown wide open.
“This junior of Murim, Sama Pyo, pays his respects to Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.”
Tall and handsome. The moment I saw him, my mouth felt as gritty as if I’d bitten into sand.
Two words had flashed through my mind.
Former fiancé.
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Sama Pyo clasped his hands in greeting to Jeok Cheongang, then nudged the hulking figure standing blankly beside him.
“What are you doing? Pay your respects.”
Tiger Giant Child Taishan, whose name and epithet fit him perfectly, bent at the waist.
“Nice to meet. Taishan saw Fire King.”
That was a new one.
I stole a glance at Jeok Cheongang. He looked ready to introduce Taishan to Yama instead of the Fire King.
Sama Pyo seemed to notice and quickly explained.
“As you may have guessed, his vocabulary is limited. That’s the best he can do.”
“...In that case, I suppose it can’t be helped.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered, looking less than pleased.
“I’ve seen some strange fellows in my time. Fine. This old man has seen you too.”
“Heh heh.”
Taishan smiled innocently and gave him two thumbs up.
“Fire King. Strong. Taishan likes strong people. Nice to meet.”
“Y-Yes. This old man is pleased to meet you too.”
“But Taishan. Hungry.”
“W-What?”
“Want to eat that. If Fire King says yes, Taishan grateful.”
His hungry eyes had already moved past our shoulders.
Jeok Cheongang spotted the refreshments on the table and nodded before he quite knew what he was doing.
“G-Go ahead.”
“Wow! Refreshments! Taishan thanks you for the food!”
Thud! Crack!
The innkeeper was going to weep tears of blood.

The enormous man charged forward, smashing what remained of the door on his way in. As though he’d been waiting for permission, Taishan swept up everything on the table. Jeok Cheongang watched him in a daze.
“Have I lived too long?”
Even Jeok Cheongang couldn’t help being taken aback.
Then again, he was used to people cowering the moment they heard the words Fire King. Aside from Cheongpung, this might be the first formidable opponent he’d encountered.
Anyway.
I scratched the back of my head and looked Sama Pyo up and down.
“So. What brings you here?”
“I have important business. If it’s all right with you, I’d rather discuss it inside.”
“It’s not all right with me.”
Sama Pyo shrugged.
“I asked out of courtesy, but you really aren’t ordinary. Do you also harbor ill feelings toward the demonic, heterodox path?”
“It’s not that, exactly...”
Damn it. Put that way, I didn’t have much of an answer.

I had only met him once, but my first impression of him had not been particularly bad. Nor was I some hardcore zealot who shouted about eradicating the heterodox path and glorifying the orthodox faction whenever I got the chance.
Jeok Cheongang didn’t seem to feel much differently.
“What are you two doing standing there? Falling for each other?”
With Jeok Cheongang saying that, I had no good reason to keep Sama Pyo out. I jerked my chin toward him.
“Damn it. Come in, then.”
“Thank you. And thank you, Great Hero Jeok.”
Sama Pyo entered with a polite bow. Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“The young brat has some manners. Or did he inherit his father’s sly streak?”
Sama Pyo paused, then smiled.
“Probably the latter. So you remember my father.”
“I’d forgotten him until I saw your face. You’re the spitting image of the Black Night King in his younger days.”
Black Night King Sima Gong.
Sama Pyo’s father, and the man who had built the Black Dragon Demon Gate into what it was today.
His epithet made him sound like one of the Ten Kings, but according to Gung Gibang, he had nothing to do with them.
Just like the Green Forest Battle King, the Green Forest Alliance Leader, and the Escort King of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
They were Supreme Peak masters whose martial prowess was beyond most people’s reach. That still wasn’t enough to make them part of the legend of the Ten Kings.
Black Night King Sima Gong, one of the greatest masters in the unorthodox martial world and the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, had apparently received the title in much the same way.
“Still...”
Jeok Cheongang studied Sama Pyo, then frowned.
“I didn’t know the Black Night King had a son so young.”
“I have seven older brothers and nine older sisters. I’m the youngest.”
“Hah. The Virility Saber King would weep if he heard that. So you’re the Young Sect Leader.”
Sama Pyo’s eyes widened slightly.
“I am, but how did you—”
“Isn’t it obvious?”
Jeok Cheongang snorted.
“Given the Black Night King’s personality, that is exactly what he would do. If your talent was sufficient, he wouldn’t care even if it meant burying all his other children alive as sacrifices.”
“He hasn’t changed much, then. You could never tell what that man was thinking. Sly as a fox and cunning as a viper.”
Look at him, casually throwing a parent insult right to his face. My heart almost swelled with awe.
The insult implied he recognized Sama Pyo’s talent, but it was still an insult. Before the dutiful son could take offense and start something, I cut in.
“So what brings you here?”
“...Hmm. Well.”
Sama Pyo’s expression was hard to read. He reached inside his robe and took something out.
Paper—a fairly expensive commodity in Murim. The words at the top caught my eye at once.
★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★
I stared at the sheet he’d laid on the table and rubbed my chin.
“This looks familiar.”
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.
“It would.”
“I don’t know who came up with it, but they’re a genius.”
“It’s rather bold, too.”
Tap.

Sama Pyo’s long finger came down on one part of the sheet: the recruitment requirements Hyuk Mujin had scrawled in his terrible handwriting. Of all the lines beneath them, he pointed to one in particular.
\# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter
His soft voice continued.
“I especially like this part.”
“So?”
“I’d like to apply. To the Two Dragons Pavilion.”
I’d suspected as much, but hearing him say it still left me with mixed feelings.
I thought for a moment, then clicked my tongue.
“Why?”
“The moment I heard the song, I had a feeling. This is exactly the place I’ve been looking for.”
“Yeah. Bullshit.”
That wasn’t even funny.
The song promised a new era of success, more sects seeking you out, and a changed life. None of that applied to Sama Pyo.

The Black Dragon Demon Gate was one of the three most powerful sects in the unorthodox martial world. Even if Sama Pyo hadn’t been its Young Sect Leader, being born the Black Night King’s son all but guaranteed him wealth and status.
And he wants to join the Two Dragons Pavilion?
Even if the orthodox faction’s diehards held up picket signs and protested, Sama Pyo was more than capable of securing a position within the Murim Alliance.
I folded my arms and stared at him.
“If this is a joke, it’s not funny.”
“Fortunately, I’m serious.”
“Cut the bullshit. What’s the real reason?”
“The notice didn’t say I had to give one.”
“Then get lost. I won’t see you out.”
Sama Pyo shrugged as though he had no choice.
“I thought that if I joined the Two Dragons Pavilion, I might be able to shed the label of belonging to the demonic, heterodox path.”
“You don’t seem all that eager to shed it.”
“Is that really how I seem?”
“I don’t trust you.”
“Fair enough. Then I’ll speak frankly.”
“Go on. Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh. Then his expression hardened.
A low voice slipped from between his perfectly smooth lips and pierced my ears.
“I intend to use you for my own benefit. Depending on the circumstances, you will become a useful card to me in one way or another.”
A heavy silence fell.
Even Taishan, who had been chewing noisily without pause, stopped moving. Hyuk Mujin stared back and forth between Sama Pyo and me with eyes as wide as lanterns.
Then someone broke the silence.
“What an interesting fellow.”
Jeok Cheongang was watching Sama Pyo with an expression I couldn’t read. Was he amused or angry? He turned to me.
“What do you think?”
I considered it for a moment.
“He makes quite an impression. I doubt this is his first interview.”
“Will you take him?”
“Hard to say.”
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo. I couldn’t tell how much of what he’d said was a joke and how much he meant.
But one thing was certain.
He’s interesting.
Tap. Tap.
The only sound echoing through the silence was the tapping of fingers against the table.
I gathered my thoughts in that brief silence and looked Sama Pyo straight in the eye.
“Let’s make one thing clear first.”
“By all means.”
“If you try anything—”
“Summary execution,” Sama Pyo said before I could finish. “I’ll remember.”
“Huh. Straight to the point.”
“It’s only natural. Are we done, then?”
“You haven’t been accepted yet. I’m only keeping you under consideration for now. For today, go.”
“Very well.”
What in the world was this man after?
I watched Sama Pyo and Taishan prepare to leave, my curiosity only growing. Then I remembered one important thing.
“And one more thing.”
“You’re paying for that guy’s food.”

With Jeok Cheongang saying that, I had no good reason to keep Sama Pyo out.
I jerked my chin toward him.
“Damn it.
Come in, then.”
“Thank you.
And thank you, Great Hero Jeok.”
Sama Pyo entered with a polite bow.
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“The young brat has some manners.
Or did he inherit his father’s sly streak?”
Sama Pyo paused, then smiled.
“Probably the latter.
So you remember my father.”
“I’d forgotten him until I saw your face.
You’re the spitting image of the Black Night King in his younger days.”
Black Night King Sima Gong.
Sama Pyo’s father, and the man who had built the Black Dragon Demon Gate into what it was today.
His epithet made him sound like one of the Ten Kings, but according to Gung Gibang, he had nothing to do with them.
Just like the Green Forest Battle King, the Green Forest Alliance Leader, and the Escort King of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
They were Supreme Peak masters whose martial prowess was beyond most people’s reach.
That still wasn’t enough to make them part of the legend of the Ten Kings.
Black Night King Sima Gong, one of the greatest masters in the unorthodox martial world and the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, had apparently received the title in much the same way.
“Still...”
Jeok Cheongang studied Sama Pyo, then frowned.
“I didn’t know the Black Night King had a son so young.”
“I have seven older brothers and nine older sisters.
I’m the youngest.”
“Hah.
The Virility Saber King would weep if he heard that.
So you’re the Young Sect Leader.”
Sama Pyo’s eyes widened slightly.
“I am, but how did you—”
“Isn’t it obvious?”
Jeok Cheongang snorted.
“Given the Black Night King’s personality, that is exactly what he would do.
If your talent was sufficient, he wouldn’t care even if it meant burying all his other children alive as sacrifices.”
“He hasn’t changed much, then.
You could never tell what that man was thinking.
Sly as a fox and cunning as a viper.”
Look at him, casually throwing a parent insult right to his face.
My heart almost swelled with awe.
The insult implied he recognized Sama Pyo’s talent, but it was still an insult.
Before the dutiful son could take offense and start something, I cut in.
“So what brings you here?”
Well.”
Sama Pyo’s expression was hard to read.
He reached inside his robe and took something out.
Paper—a fairly expensive commodity in Murim.
The words at the top caught my eye at once.
★I Was a Nameless Foot Soldier, but in the Two Dragons Pavilion, I’m a Murim Hero?!★
I stared at the sheet he’d laid on the table and rubbed my chin.
“This looks familiar.”
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.
“It would.”
“I don’t know who came up with it, but they’re a genius.”
“It’s rather bold, too.”
Tap.
Sama Pyo’s long finger came down on one part of the sheet: the recruitment requirements Hyuk Mujin had scrawled in his terrible handwriting.
Of all the lines beneath them, he pointed to one in particular.
\# Gender and sect affiliation don’t matter
His soft voice continued.
“I especially like this part.”
“So?”
“I’d like to apply.
To the Two Dragons Pavilion.”
I’d suspected as much, but hearing him say it still left me with mixed feelings.
I thought for a moment, then clicked my tongue.
“Why?”
“The moment I heard the song, I had a feeling.
This is exactly the place I’ve been looking for.”
“Yeah.
Bullshit.”
That wasn’t even funny.
The song promised a new era of success, more sects seeking you out, and a changed life.
None of that applied to Sama Pyo.
The Black Dragon Demon Gate was one of the three most powerful sects in the unorthodox martial world.
Even if Sama Pyo hadn’t been its Young Sect Leader, being born the Black Night King’s son all but guaranteed him wealth and status.
And he wants to join the Two Dragons Pavilion?
Even if the orthodox faction’s diehards held up picket signs and protested, Sama Pyo was more than capable of securing a position within the Murim Alliance.
I folded my arms and stared at him.
“If this is a joke, it’s not funny.”
“Fortunately, I’m serious.”
“Cut the bullshit.
What’s the real reason?”
“The notice didn’t say I had to give one.”
“Then get lost.
I won’t see you out.”
Sama Pyo shrugged as though he had no choice.
“I thought that if I joined the Two Dragons Pavilion, I might be able to shed the label of belonging to the demonic, heterodox path.”
“You don’t seem all that eager to shed it.”
“Is that really how I seem?”
“I don’t trust you.”
“Fair enough.
Then I’ll speak frankly.”
“Go on.
Unless you want the shit beaten out of you.”
Sama Pyo gave a quiet laugh.
Then his expression hardened.
A low voice slipped from between his perfectly smooth lips and pierced my ears.
“I intend to use you for my own benefit.
Depending on the circumstances, you will become a useful card to me in one way or another.”
A heavy silence fell.
Even Taishan, who had been chewing noisily without pause, stopped moving.
Hyuk Mujin stared back and forth between Sama Pyo and me with eyes as wide as lanterns.
Then someone broke the silence.
“What an interesting fellow.”
Jeok Cheongang was watching Sama Pyo with an expression I couldn’t read.
Was he amused or angry?
He turned to me.
“What do you think?”
I considered it for a moment.
“He makes quite an impression.
I doubt this is his first interview.”
“Will you take him?”
“Hard to say.”
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo.
I couldn’t tell how much of what he’d said was a joke and how much he meant.
But one thing was certain.
He’s interesting.
Tap.
Tap.
The only sound echoing through the silence was the tapping of fingers against the table.
I gathered my thoughts in that brief silence and looked Sama Pyo straight in the eye.
“Let’s make one thing clear first.”
“By all means.”
“If you try anything—”
“Summary execution,” Sama Pyo said before I could finish.
“I’ll remember.”
“Huh.
Straight to the point.”
“It’s only natural.
Are we done, then?”
“You haven’t been accepted yet.
I’m only keeping you under consideration for now.
For today, go.”
“Very well.”
What in the world was this man after?
I watched Sama Pyo and Taishan prepare to leave, my curiosity only growing.
Then I remembered one important thing.
“And one more thing.”
“You’re paying for that guy’s food.”

chapters.title: Chapter 543
paragraphs: Thud. Thud.
Footsteps shook the ground, and people on the street moved aside to clear a path.
Black Dragon Saber Sama Pyo knew the wary looks were not because of Taishan walking beside him.
The rumors about us have spread, then.
It would have been stranger if they hadn’t.
A grimy yellow knot protruded from the belt of a beggar dozing against an alley wall. Faint calluses marked the palm of a stallkeeper swatting at flies.
The Beggars’ Sect. The Lower District Sect.
And those were only the ones he could spot at a glance.
Countless eyes watched him wherever he went in Henan. Before half a day had passed, word of what he had done today would reach any number of people.
Not that I intended to hide it.
Trying to conceal his movements would only invite greater suspicion. Sama Pyo had no intention of ruining things through half-baked caution.
—My lord.
Taishan’s cautious Sound Transmission reached his ear. Without showing any reaction, Sama Pyo pointed to a small noodle shop off to one side.
“I’m in the mood for thin noodles today. Shall we stop for a bowl?”
“Hm?”
“You must be full. Say so if you don’t want any.”
“No! Taishan likes noodles!”
“You should have said so. Excuse me. Ten bowls of thin noodles... No, make that twenty.”
The middle-aged woman running the shop looked as though she doubted her ears.
“...How many bowls did you say?”

Sama Pyo had chosen the noodle shop for a simple reason. Perhaps because of its poor location, it had no other customers. They could sit with their backs to the street and exchange Sound Transmissions out of everyone else’s sight.
It also helped that the owner appeared to be an ordinary commoner with no connection to Murim.
“Twenty bowls. As you can see, I have a hungry ghost with me.”
“Y-Yes!”
It must have been an unexpected windfall for her. As her eyes lit up and she hurried to work, Sama Pyo barely moved his lips.
—You had something to say.
The small chair creaked under Taishan’s weight. Balanced precariously on it, he answered.
—My lord. Taishan worried.
—About what?
—Did not obey Sect Leader’s orders. Taishan worried about my lord.
A bitter smile touched Sama Pyo’s lips.
—I wondered if that might be the reason. So it was because of that person after all.
—Disobeying bad. Sect Leader gets angry. My lord in danger.
—Yes. He is more than capable of that.
Sama Pyo looked down at the chopsticks neatly arranged on the table.
They brought to mind his father, Black Night King Sima Gong. A man with no paternal affection whatsoever.
He probably thinks of his children as chopsticks.
Replace one when it falls on the ground. Put it away when it no longer pleases him.
His seven older brothers and nine older sisters had been discarded that way. Sama Pyo was the last—and best-made—chopstick the Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate had chosen.
And even I might be replaced someday.

His father was well past eighty, but his appetite and libido were as vigorous as ever. Three wives and four concubines had not been enough for him; he had taken more than ten concubines in all. Sama Pyo had no shortage of blood relatives, older or younger.
But—
—Don’t worry.
—Hm?
Sama Pyo took a sip of the lukewarm water the owner had brought him.
—He is heartless. That is precisely why he cannot easily cast me aside.
Black Night King Sima Gong was indeed a heartless man. He could set aside parental affection and assess reality with a cold eye.
By the same logic, there was no other successor who could replace Sama Pyo, whose martial talent surpassed even Sima Gong’s in his younger days and whose calculating mind ran deep.
Besides...
—There will be no punishment. I’ve taken a different route, but it still leads where my father wants to go.
—My lord. Taishan does not understand. Taishan is stupid.
Sama Pyo smiled at Taishan, who could only tilt his head in confusion.
—You don’t need to understand. Just stay by my side. All right?
—Taishan listens to my lord. Taishan is good.
Taishan nodded vigorously. Just then, the owner began setting bowls piled high with thin noodles on the table.
“Careful, they’re hot. Take your time—”
“Wow! Taishan! Thank you for the food!”
“Oh my goodness!”
The owner stared in shock as Taishan lifted a bowl of steaming noodles and gulped them down.
Sama Pyo let out a quiet laugh at the sight. Then his face went rigid.
“Hmm.”
Taishan looked up from his noodles.
“My lord. What is it?”
“My lord?”
Still staring at something, Sama Pyo murmured, “No. Nothing. I must have seen wrong.”
But he knew he had not mistaken the person who had passed by. He knew what that person’s presence meant, too.
“...Perhaps I should have just obeyed the order.”
“Hm? My lord. What did you say?”
Sama Pyo answered with a sigh. Taishan already had the last bowl in his hands.
“You shameless glutton. Finish stuffing your face.”
“Wow! Taishan will give his life for my lord!”
“Here you go.”
A voice clearer and lovelier than a Young Chang piano. A hand held out two bamboo slips to me.
What’s going on?

Less than half an hour had passed since the two uninvited guests from the Black Dragon Demon Gate had left and Jeok Cheongang had gone to the latrine. Now another unexpected visitor had appeared, and this one left me at a loss.
I blinked at her, then finally managed to speak.
“W-What are these?”
“Applications.”
Ju Hwaran looked as though she wondered why I had to ask. “One for me and one for Captain Song.”
Behind her, Song Ilseom muttered, “I never agreed to this.”
“I hired you, didn’t I? If you’re my escort, of course you have to come with me.”
“This wasn’t in the contract. It’s a breach of contract. If I join the Murim Alliance, I’ll need hazard pay...”
“I’ll pay you double.”
“Then that’s a different story.”
Maybe it was all the money she had wrung out of the Zhongnan Sect. Ju Hwaran was showing off the sort of easy spending only someone young and rich could manage.
Watching her, though, I felt as stifled as if I’d stepped into a greenhouse in midsummer.
“So. You’re serious?”
“Yes. I am.”
Ju Hwaran nodded without hesitation and met my eyes.
“I want to join the Two Dragons Pavilion.”
I had suspected as much, but hearing Ju Hwaran say it herself left my mouth dry. I thought for a moment before speaking.
“I won’t accept you just because we know each other.”
“If I’d planned to rely on our connection from the start, I would’ve come without an application, wouldn’t I?”
She smiled. I sighed inwardly.
“It’ll be dangerous. Very dangerous.”

“I know. The Two Dragons Pavilion is directly under the Alliance Leader’s Office, and unlike the other pavilions, it cannot even command its own squads or battalions. It will probably function more like a special operations detachment.”
Exactly right.

Mae Jonghak wanted to deploy Cheongpung and me, two considerable assets even within the Murim Alliance, as a small detached force. It was also why most of the leadership had agreed to the arrangement.
“Young Lady Ju, if you know that, why—”
“Great Hero Jin.”
Ju Hwaran cut me off.
“Did you say that to the other applicants?”
“What?”
“That it’s dangerous. Did you ask why they were applying when they knew that?”
Her quiet voice went on.
“It’s strange. You put up a notice because you needed people, and now you’re trying to talk me out of it.”
“That’s...”
She gave a quiet laugh when I hesitated.
“You don’t have an answer, do you?”
She had me there. I scratched the back of my head and reluctantly nodded.
“Honestly? No, I don’t.”
“I came here as a martial artist. I’d like you to judge me as one.”
“As you are...”
“I might fall far short by your standards, but I’m a swordswoman who has reached the Peak realm.”
“Since we’re being honest, you do fall pretty far short. Song Ilseom might be another story.”
Poke.
Hyuk Mujin, who had been watching with bated breath, gave me a discreet jab in the ribs.
He needn’t have worried. Ju Hwaran’s gaze did not waver.
“Even compared with the other applicants?”
“I can’t say for certain, but probably.”
“What about experience?”
“Experience?”
“I started accompanying my father on escort runs when I was twelve. In experience and knowledge of the land, I don’t think I fall short of any seasoned veteran of the martial world.”

She had a point. Ju Hwaran had been heir to the Yongbong Escort Bureau, once among the most renowned escort bureaus in the world. For the past several years, she had even run it herself after her father collapsed from qi deviation.
I can’t dismiss the experience she gained from that.
Escort bureaus traveled far and wide. To complete their assignments on time, they used whatever means they could, learning the roads and gathering information wherever they went.
And during the Great Faction War, Ju Hwaran’s grandfather, the Escort King, had completed his legendary Ten-Thousand-Li Journey while evading the Demonic Cult’s countless watchers.
“Great Hero Jin.”
Her powerful voice pierced my ears.

“I have no intention of becoming a burden. But please think about this objectively. Set aside everything that’s happened between us until now. Are Captain Song and I truly of no use to the Two Dragons Pavilion?”
“I’m fully prepared for what this entails. Even if you reject me, I’ll accept it.”
I closed my eyes.
Ju Hwaran was right. This was something I had to consider coldly.
The person waiting for my answer was not the woman I had walked beside one night in a garden where the flowers were just beginning to bloom.
Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.
She was a martial artist skilled enough to be counted among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, and the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
She also had abilities we would need on the missions ahead, given that the Two Dragons Pavilion would operate as a detached force.
Then why?
Why did I hate admitting it? Why did I want to stop her, even if I had to be unreasonable?
“Um, Captain.”
I opened my eyes. Hyuk Mujin watched me nervously before going on.
“I think you’ve forgotten something.”
“What?”
“All the other applicants ran away. Every last one. They probably won’t come back tomorrow or the day after, either.”
“I know, you punk. Old Man Ilyang got carried out of here half-paralyzed. So?”
“No, I mean... that’s all I wanted to say.”
Hyuk Mujin flinched and turned his head away.
But I understood him perfectly.
“Whew.”
I sighed and looked straight at Ju Hwaran.
“Before I answer, there’s one thing you should know, Young Lady Ju.”
How was I supposed to bring it up? As I hesitated, she smiled.
“It doesn’t matter.”
“What?”
“I saw them on my way here. With someone that big beside him, how could I miss them? And from what people were whispering, I could more or less tell where they’d come from.”
Ju Hwaran continued calmly.
“Why would that be a problem?”
“I think I’ve given you enough time to consider it. May I have your answer?”
I studied her. The tangle in my head seemed to have cleared.
Or perhaps it hadn’t, not entirely.
But right now, at least, I knew what I had to say.
“Yes. All right.”
A bright smile spread across Ju Hwaran’s face.
